weeks.title: Clauses and complex sentences
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki clause kya hota hai, main aur dependent clause mein fark kya hai, aur unhe jod kar compound aur complex sentences kaise bante hain.
concepts: **Clause**: words ka aisa group jisme ek subject aur ek verb dono ho. 'She smiled' ek clause hai, par 'in the morning' clause nahi hai kyunki usme verb nahi hai.
**Independent (main) clause**: akele hi complete sentence ban jaata hai. Jaise 'The bus was late.' Iska meaning poora hai.

**Dependent (subordinate) clause**: akele poora meaning nahi deta, main clause ka sahara chahiye. Ye aksar because, although, when, if, since, unless jaise **subordinating conjunctions** se shuru hota hai. Jaise 'because the bus was late' sunke lagta hai baat adhuri hai.
**Noun clause**: sentence mein noun ka kaam karta hai (subject ya object). 'What he said surprised me' mein 'What he said' subject hai.
**Adjective (relative) clause**: kisi noun ke baare mein extra jaankari deta hai, who, which, that, whose se shuru hota hai. 'The book that I borrowed is missing.'
**Adverb clause**: time, reason, condition, contrast (concession) batata hai. 'Even though it was late, she finished the report' mein contrast hai.
**Simple, compound, complex**: Simple = ek main clause. Compound = do main clauses jo and, but, or, so se jude hon. Complex = ek main clause + kam se kam ek dependent clause.

**Defining vs non-defining relative clause**: Defining clause batata hai kaunsa noun (no commas). Non-defining clause sirf extra info deta hai, isliye commas mein aata hai aur usme 'that' use nahi hota, 'which' ya 'who' hota hai.

example.problem: Do sentences ko ek complex sentence mein jodiye: 'The laptop was expensive. Riya bought it last week.'
steps: Dono sentences mein common cheez dhoondho: 'The laptop' aur 'it' ek hi cheez hai.
Doosre sentence ko relative clause banana hai, toh 'it' ki jagah relative pronoun lagao: 'that Riya bought last week'.
Ye clause batata hai kaunsa laptop, isliye ye defining clause hai, commas nahi lagenge.
Clause ko noun 'The laptop' ke turant baad rakho.
Answer: **The laptop that Riya bought last week was expensive.**

mistakes: 'Although' aur 'but' ek saath lagana: 'Although it rained, but we played' galat hai. Ek hi conjunction rakho: 'Although it rained, we played.'
Do main clauses ko sirf comma se jodna (**comma splice**): 'I was tired, I slept early' galat hai. Full stop, semicolon ya 'so' use karo.
Non-defining clause mein 'that' likhna: 'Delhi, that is the capital, ...' galat hai, 'which' likho.
revision: Clause = subject + verb.
Main clause akela khada ho sakta hai, dependent clause nahi.
Compound = main + main (and, but, so); complex = main + dependent.
Noun clause, adjective clause, adverb clause: kaam ke hisaab se naam.
Non-defining clause commas mein aata hai aur 'that' nahi leta.
Although/though ke saath 'but' mat lagao.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dependent clause?
options: The train left early
because the train left early
The passengers were angry
Trains run daily
questions.explanation: 'because the train left early' mein subject aur verb hai, par 'because' ki wajah se ye akele complete meaning nahi deta, isliye dependent clause hai. Baaki teeno options akele complete sentence hain, yaani independent clauses.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'I wanted to call you, but my phone died.'
options: Simple
Complex
Compound-complex
Compound
questions.explanation: 'I wanted to call you' aur 'my phone died' dono main clauses hain aur coordinating conjunction 'but' se jude hain, toh ye compound sentence hai. Complex tab hota jab ek clause dependent hota (jaise 'because my phone died').

questions.question: In the sentence 'What she proposed surprised the whole team', the clause 'What she proposed' works as:
options: a noun clause acting as the subject
an adjective clause describing 'team'
an adverb clause of reason
an independent clause
questions.explanation: Poocho 'kisne surprise kiya?' Jawab: 'What she proposed'. Ye verb 'surprised' ka subject hai, isliye noun clause hai. Ye kisi noun ko describe nahi kar raha, toh adjective clause nahi hai, aur akele complete bhi nahi hai.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Delhi which is India's capital has many museums.
Delhi, that is India's capital, has many museums.
Delhi, which is India's capital, has many museums.
Delhi, which is India's capital has many museums.
questions.explanation: Delhi ek hi hai, toh 'which is India's capital' sirf extra info hai, yaani non-defining clause. Isliye dono taraf comma chahiye aur 'which' use hoga. Option B mein 'that' galat hai, aur option D mein closing comma missing hai.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Although he studied hard, but he failed the test.
Although he studied hard, he failed the test.
He studied hard, he failed the test.
Although studied hard, he failed the test.
questions.explanation: 'Although' pehle se contrast dikha raha hai, isliye 'but' ki zarurat nahi. Option A mein double conjunction hai, option C comma splice hai, aur option D mein dependent clause ka subject 'he' gayab hai.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of concession (contrast)?
options: Even though the road was wet, the bus kept its speed.
Because the road was wet, the bus slowed down.
The road that we took was wet.
If the road is wet, drive slowly.
questions.explanation: Concession matlab 'aisa hone ke bawajood'. 'Even though the road was wet' ke bawajood bus ki speed kam nahi hui, ye contrast hai. 'Because' reason dikhata hai, 'If' condition, aur 'that we took' adjective clause hai. Trap: 'Because' wala bhi adverb clause hai, par reason ka, concession ka nahi.

questions.question: Which of the following is a clause?
options: in the morning
after the long lecture
the students left
with a heavy bag
questions.explanation: Clause ke liye subject aur verb dono chahiye. 'the students left' mein subject 'the students' aur verb 'left' hai, isliye ye clause hai. 'after the long lecture' clause jaisa lagta hai kyunki 'after' se shuru hota hai, par isme koi verb nahi hai, toh ye sirf phrase hai. Baaki dono mein bhi verb nahi hai.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'The match was cancelled because the ground was wet.'
options: Simple
Complex
Compound
Compound-complex
questions.explanation: 'The match was cancelled' main clause hai aur 'because the ground was wet' dependent clause hai jo reason batata hai. Main + dependent = complex sentence. Compound tab hota jab dono clauses main hote aur and/but/so se jude hote.

questions.question: In 'The phone that I bought online stopped working', the clause 'that I bought online' is:
options: a noun clause acting as the subject of 'stopped'
an adverb clause of time
an independent clause
an adjective (relative) clause describing 'phone'
questions.explanation: 'that I bought online' batata hai kaunsa phone, yaani noun 'phone' ke baare mein jaankari deta hai, isliye adjective (relative) clause hai. Sentence ka subject 'The phone' hai, ye clause nahi, aur ye clause akele complete sentence bhi nahi ban sakta.

questions.question: Join the two sentences into one complex sentence without changing the meaning: 'Kabir missed the bus. He woke up late.'
options: Kabir missed the bus because he woke up late.
Kabir missed the bus, he woke up late.
Kabir missed the bus, and he woke up late.
Because Kabir missed the bus, he woke up late.
questions.explanation: Late uthna reason hai aur bus chhootna result, isliye 'because' reason wale clause 'he woke up late' ke saath lagega. 'Because Kabir missed the bus, he woke up late' bhi complex hai, par usme cause aur result ulte ho gaye. Sirf comma wala option comma splice hai, aur 'and' wala sentence compound hai, complex nahi.

questions.question: In 'Nobody knows where the keys are', the clause 'where the keys are' works as:
options: a noun clause, the object of 'knows'
an adverb clause of place
an adjective clause describing 'Nobody'
an independent clause
questions.explanation: Poocho 'Nobody kya jaanta hai?' Jawab: 'where the keys are'. Ye verb 'knows' ka object hai, isliye noun clause hai. Trap 'adverb clause of place' hai kyunki clause 'where' se shuru hota hai, par ye kisi action ki jagah nahi bata raha, 'knows' ka object hai.

questions.question: Compare: (a) 'My brother who lives in Pune is a doctor.' (b) 'My brother, who lives in Pune, is a doctor.' Which statement is correct?
options: (a) and (b) mean exactly the same; the commas change nothing.
(a) suggests only one brother; (b) suggests more than one brother.
(b) is wrong because 'who' cannot begin a non-defining clause.
(a) suggests more than one brother; (b) suggests only one brother.
questions.explanation: (a) mein commas nahi hain, toh ye defining clause hai: batata hai kaunsa brother (Pune wala), yaani speaker ke ek se zyada brothers hain. (b) mein commas hain, toh ye non-defining clause hai: sirf extra info, yaani brother ek hi hai. Ulta wala option sabse bada trap hai. Non-defining clause 'who' se shuru ho sakta hai, sirf 'that' mana hai.

questions.question: Which of the following is a complex sentence?
options: After the lecture, we went to the canteen.
After the lecture ended, we went to the canteen.
The lecture ended, and we went to the canteen.
We left the lecture hall and went to the canteen.
questions.explanation: 'After the lecture ended' mein subject 'the lecture' aur verb 'ended' hai, aur 'After' ise dependent banata hai. Main clause 'we went to the canteen' ke saath milkar ye complex sentence hai. Trap 'After the lecture,' hai: isme verb nahi, toh ye phrase hai aur sentence simple hai. 'and' wala sentence compound hai, aur aakhri sentence mein ek hi subject 'We' ke do verbs hain, toh wo bhi simple hai.

questions.question: Which sentence contains BOTH a noun clause and an adjective clause?
options: I know that the girl who won the quiz is from Kerala.
The girl who won the quiz is from Kerala.
I know that the girl is from Kerala.
When the girl from Kerala won the quiz, everyone in the hall clapped.
questions.explanation: Pehle sentence mein 'that the girl ... is from Kerala' verb 'know' ka object hai (noun clause), aur uske andar 'who won the quiz' noun 'girl' ko describe karta hai (adjective clause). Doosre mein sirf adjective clause hai, teesre mein sirf noun clause, aur 'When the girl from Kerala won the quiz' adverb clause of time hai.

questions.question: Which sentence changes 'Even though the tickets were expensive, the show was sold out.' into a correct compound sentence with the same meaning?
options: The tickets were expensive, so the show was sold out.
Although the tickets were expensive, but the show was sold out.
The tickets were expensive, but the show was sold out.
The tickets were expensive, the show was sold out.
questions.explanation: Original mein contrast hai (mehenge tickets ke bawajood show full). Compound sentence ke liye do main clauses ko coordinating conjunction se jodo, aur contrast ke liye 'but' sahi hai. 'so' result batata hai, jo meaning badal deta hai. 'Although ... but' double conjunction hai, aur sirf comma wala option comma splice hai.

weeks.title: Active and passive voice
weeks.summary: Is week aap sentence ko active se passive mein badalna seekhoge, har tense mein 'be' ka sahi form lagana, aur samjhoge ki formal writing mein passive kab useful hai.
concepts: **Active voice**: subject khud action karta hai. 'The chef cooked the meal.' Yahan chef karta hai.
**Passive voice**: action jis par hua (object) wo subject ban jaata hai. 'The meal was cooked by the chef.' Passive voice mein object subject ban jaata hai.
**Formula**: object + correct form of **be** + **V3 (past participle)** + (by + doer). Tense 'be' se dikhta hai: is/are, was/were, has been, will be, is being, was being.
**Agent (by phrase)** optional hai: agar doer unknown ya unimportant ho toh hata do. 'My phone was stolen' kaafi hai, 'by someone' likhne ki zarurat nahi.
**Intransitive verbs** (jinke saath object nahi hota: arrive, sleep, happen, die) ka passive nahi banta.
**Modals ka passive**: modal + be + V3. 'You must sign the form' banega 'The form must be signed.'
**Question ka passive**: 'Who wrote this?' banega 'By whom was this written?' Helping verb subject se pehle aata hai.
**Kab use karein**: process describe karte waqt, reports aur scientific writing mein, ya jab result doer se zyada important ho. 'The samples were tested at 40 °C.'

example.problem: Passive voice mein badliye: 'The committee will announce the results tomorrow.'
steps: Subject = 'The committee', verb = 'will announce', object = 'the results'.
Object 'the results' ko subject ki jagah le aao.
Tense simple future hai, toh 'be' ka form 'will be' hoga.
Main verb 'announce' ka V3 = 'announced'.
'tomorrow' jaisa time word waise hi rehta hai; doer optional hai.
Answer: **The results will be announced (by the committee) tomorrow.**

mistakes: 'be' ka galat tense: 'They are building a flat' ka passive 'A flat is built' nahi, 'A flat is being built' hai. Continuous ke liye 'being' zaroori hai.
Intransitive verb ka passive banana: 'The guests were arrived' galat hai. 'arrive' ka object hi nahi hai.
V3 ki jagah V1 ya V2 lagana: 'The form must be submit' galat, 'must be submitted' sahi.
revision: Passive = object + be + V3 (+ by agent).
Tense 'be' ke form se dikhta hai, main verb hamesha V3.
Continuous tense mein 'being' aata hai: is being / was being.
Perfect tense mein 'been' aata hai: has been / had been.
Intransitive verbs ka passive nahi banta.
Unknown doer ho toh 'by someone' hata do.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'Meena writes a letter.'
options: A letter was written by Meena.
A letter is being written by Meena.
A letter is written by Meena.
A letter has been written by Meena.
questions.explanation: Active simple present hai ('writes'), toh passive mein 'is + V3' aayega: 'is written'. 'was written' past ho gaya, 'is being' continuous ho gaya, aur 'has been' perfect. Tense badalna nahi chahiye.

questions.question: Which sentence CANNOT be changed into the passive voice?
options: The guests arrived late.
The guests ate the snacks.
The guests praised the host.
The guests signed the register.
questions.explanation: 'arrive' intransitive verb hai, iska koi object nahi hai, isliye passive nahi banta. Baaki sab mein object hai (snacks, host, register), jaise 'The host was praised by the guests.'

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'They are repairing the bridge.'
options: The bridge is repaired by them.
The bridge was being repaired by them.
The bridge has been repaired by them.
The bridge is being repaired by them.
questions.explanation: 'are repairing' present continuous hai, toh passive 'is being + V3' banega. Sabse common trap option A hai jisme 'being' chhoot gaya, jisse tense simple present ban jaata hai.

questions.question: Choose the best passive form of: 'Someone has stolen my bag.'
options: My bag was stolen by someone.
My bag has been stolen.
My bag has stolen.
My bag had been stolen.
questions.explanation: 'has stolen' present perfect hai, toh passive 'has been stolen'. Doer 'someone' unknown hai isliye hata diya. Option A mein tense past ho gaya, option C mein 'been' missing hai, aur option D past perfect hai.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'You must submit the form by Friday.'
options: The form must submitted by Friday.
The form must be submit by Friday.
The form must been submitted by Friday.
The form must be submitted by Friday.
questions.explanation: Modal ka passive = modal + be + V3, yaani 'must be submitted'. Option A mein 'be' nahi hai, option B mein V3 nahi hai, aur option C mein 'been' galat hai kyunki modal ke baad base form 'be' aata hai.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of the question: 'Who wrote this report?'
options: Who was this report written?
By whom this report was written?
By whom was this report written?
Who has written this report by?
questions.explanation: 'Who' doer hai, toh passive mein 'By whom' banega. Question hai, isliye helping verb 'was' subject 'this report' se pehle aayega: 'By whom was this report written?' Option B mein word order statement jaisa hai, jo question ke liye galat hai.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'The police caught the thief.'
options: The thief was caught by the police.
The thief is caught by the police.
The thief was catched by the police.
The thief has been caught by the police.
questions.explanation: 'caught' simple past hai, toh passive 'was + V3' banega: 'was caught'. 'catch' ka V3 'caught' hai, 'catched' koi word nahi. 'is caught' present ho gaya aur 'has been caught' present perfect, dono mein tense badal gaya.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The workers built the bridge in 2019.
The bridge was built in 2019.
The bridge looks old now.
The workers were building the bridge.
questions.explanation: Passive mein 'be' + V3 hota hai aur jis par action hua wo subject hota hai: 'The bridge was built'. Trap 'The workers were building the bridge' hai: isme 'were' hai, par uske baad V-ing hai aur workers khud action kar rahe hain, toh ye active past continuous hai.

questions.question: In the passive voice, which form of the main verb is always used?
options: V1 (base form)
V2 (simple past form)
V-ing form
V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: Passive ka formula hai object + be + V3. Tense 'be' ke form se dikhta hai (is, was, has been, is being), par main verb hamesha V3 rehta hai. Continuous passive mein bhi 'being' ke baad V3 aata hai: 'is being written', 'is being write' nahi.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'The team had completed the project before the deadline.'
options: The project has been completed by the team before the deadline.
The project was completed by the team before the deadline.
The project had been completed by the team before the deadline.
The project had completed by the team before the deadline.
questions.explanation: 'had completed' past perfect hai, toh passive 'had been + V3' banega: 'had been completed'. 'has been' present perfect hai aur 'was completed' simple past, dono mein tense badal gaya. 'had completed' mein 'been' missing hai, isliye wo passive bana hi nahi.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'The students were decorating the hall.'
options: The hall was decorated by the students.
The hall was being decorated by the students.
The hall is being decorated by the students.
The hall were being decorated by the students.
questions.explanation: 'were decorating' past continuous hai, toh passive 'was being + V3' hoga. Naya subject 'The hall' singular hai, isliye 'were' nahi, 'was' aayega. 'was decorated' mein 'being' chhoot gaya, aur 'is being' se tense present ho gaya.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of: 'The shopkeeper has sold all the mangoes.'
options: All the mangoes has been sold by the shopkeeper.
All the mangoes were sold by the shopkeeper.
All the mangoes have sold by the shopkeeper.
All the mangoes have been sold by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation: Present perfect ka passive 'has/have been + V3' hai. Active mein 'has' tha kyunki subject 'The shopkeeper' singular tha, par passive mein naya subject 'All the mangoes' plural hai, toh 'have been sold' hoga. Trap 'has been sold' hai jisme purane subject ka verb form copy ho gaya. 'were sold' mein tense badal gaya aur 'have sold' mein 'been' missing hai.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of the question: 'Did the committee accept the proposal?'
options: Did the proposal accepted by the committee?
Was the proposal accepted by the committee?
Was the proposal accept by the committee?
Has the proposal been accepted by the committee?
questions.explanation: 'Did ... accept' simple past hai, toh passive mein 'was + V3' aayega. Yes/no question hai, isliye 'was' subject 'the proposal' se pehle jaayega: 'Was the proposal accepted ...?' Passive mein 'did' nahi rehta, isliye 'Did the proposal accepted' galat hai. 'accept' V1 hai, V3 nahi, aur 'Has ... been' se tense present perfect ho gaya.

questions.question: Choose the best passive form of: 'Someone should have informed the parents.'
options: The parents should have informed.
The parents should be informed.
The parents should have been informed.
The parents should had been informed.
questions.explanation: Modal ke baad perfect form hai: 'should have + V3'. Passive mein 'been' judega: should have been + V3 = 'should have been informed'. Doer 'Someone' unknown hai, isliye hata diya. 'should have informed' active hi reh gaya (meaning ulta: parents ne inform kiya), 'should be informed' mein past ka sense chala gaya, aur modal ke baad 'had' kabhi nahi aata.

questions.question: Which active sentence has this passive form: 'The results are being checked by two examiners.'?
options: Two examiners are checking the results.
Two examiners check the results.
Two examiners have checked the results.
Two examiners were checking the results.
questions.explanation: Passive mein 'are being + V3' present continuous dikhata hai, toh active bhi present continuous hoga. Agent 'two examiners' subject banega aur 'the results' object: 'Two examiners are checking the results.' 'check' simple present hai, 'have checked' present perfect, aur 'were checking' past continuous.

weeks.title: Direct and reported speech
weeks.summary: Is week aap kisi ki kahi hui baat ko reported speech mein likhna seekhoge: tense backshift, pronoun aur time words ka badlaav, aur questions aur commands ko report karna.
concepts: **Direct speech**: exact words quotes mein: Anu said, 'I am busy.' **Reported (indirect) speech**: baat apne shabdon mein: Anu said that she was busy.
**Backshift**: reporting verb past mein ho (said, told) toh tense ek step peeche jaata hai: am/is → was, will → would, has done → had done, did → had done.
**Pronoun change**: speaker ke hisaab se I/my badal jaate hain. 'I' → he/she, 'my' → his/her.
**Time aur place words**: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the previous day, now → then, here → there, this → that.
**Said vs told**: 'told' ke baad person (object) zaroori hai: 'She told me'. 'said' ke baad direct object nahi aata: 'She said me' galat hai.
**Questions**: yes/no question → if/whether; wh-question → wh-word wahi rehta hai. Dono mein word order statement jaisa hota hai: 'He asked where I lived', 'where did I live' nahi.
**Commands aur requests**: told/asked/ordered + object + **to-infinitive**. Negative mein 'not to': 'He told me not to wait.'
**Universal truth / scientific fact**: tense nahi badalta: 'The teacher said that water boils at 100 °C.'

example.problem: Reported speech mein badliye: Priya said, 'I am preparing for my exam today.'
steps: Reporting verb 'said' past mein hai, toh backshift hoga.
'I' → 'she' aur 'my' → 'her' (Priya female hai).
'am preparing' (present continuous) → 'was preparing' (past continuous).
'today' → 'that day'.
Quotes hata kar 'that' se jodo.
Answer: **Priya said that she was preparing for her exam that day.**

mistakes: Reported question mein question wala word order rakhna: 'She asked where was I going' galat. Sahi: 'She asked where I was going.'
'said' ke baad seedha person likhna: 'He said me to sit' galat. Sahi: 'He told me to sit' ya 'He asked me to sit'.
Baat baad mein report karte waqt bhi 'tomorrow' rakhna, jabki wo din guzar chuka hai. Waise case mein 'the next day' likho.
revision: Past reporting verb → tense ek step peeche.
told + person; said + no person.
Questions: if/whether ya wh-word + statement order, end mein full stop.
Commands: told/asked + object + (not) to + V1.
today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.
Universal truth mein tense same rehta hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: Rahul said, 'I am tired.'
options: Rahul said that he was tired.
Rahul said that I was tired.
Rahul told that he is tired.
Rahul said that he has been tired.
questions.explanation: 'am' → 'was' (backshift) aur 'I' → 'he'. Option B mein pronoun nahi badla, option C mein 'told' ke baad person missing hai, aur option D mein tense galat badla.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She said me to wait.
She told to me to wait.
She told me to wait.
She said to wait me.
questions.explanation: Command report karte waqt 'told + person + to-infinitive' aata hai: 'She told me to wait.' 'said me' galat hai, aur 'told to me' mein extra 'to' hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: He asked, 'Where do you live?'
options: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where do I live.
He asked me that where I lived.
questions.explanation: Reported question mein 'do/did' hat jaata hai aur word order statement jaisa ho jaata hai: 'where I lived'. 'do you live' backshift hoke 'I lived' bana. Option D mein wh-word ke saath 'that' extra hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: The teacher said, 'The earth revolves around the sun.'
options: The teacher said that the earth had revolved around the sun.
The teacher told that the earth revolves around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth is revolving around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
questions.explanation: Ye universal truth hai, isliye tense present hi rehta hai: 'revolves'. Option A mein past perfect ho gaya jo galat hai, option B mein 'told' ke baad person nahi hai, aur option C mein tense continuous kar diya jo original mein tha hi nahi.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: She asked, 'Have you finished the assignment?'
options: She asked whether I had finished the assignment.
She asked that had I finished the assignment.
She asked if I have finished the assignment?
She asked whether had I finished the assignment.
questions.explanation: Yes/no question hai, toh 'whether' (ya 'if') lagega. 'have finished' backshift hoke 'had finished' bana, aur order statement jaisa 'I had finished'. Option C mein tense nahi badla aur question mark galat hai; option D mein word order question jaisa reh gaya.

questions.question: On a Friday, Arjun said, 'I will send the file tomorrow.' A week later you report it. Which version is best?
options: Arjun said that he will send the file tomorrow.
Arjun said that he would send the file the next day.
Arjun said that he would send the file tomorrow.
Arjun said that I would send the file the next day.
questions.explanation: Ek hafte baad 'tomorrow' ka matlab badal gaya hai, isliye 'the next day' likhna padega. 'will' → 'would' backshift hoga aur 'I' → 'he'. Option C mein tense sahi hai par 'tomorrow' ab galat din batata hai, ye sabse bada trap hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: Sana said to me, 'I will call you.'
options: Sana told that she would call me.
Sana said me that she would call me.
Sana told me that she would call me.
Sana told me that I would call her.
questions.explanation: 'said to me' reported speech mein 'told me' ban jaata hai. 'will' → 'would', 'I' (Sana) → 'she', aur 'you' (main) → 'me'. 'told' ke baad person chahiye, isliye 'Sana told that' galat hai; 'said me' bhi galat hai. Aakhri option mein pronouns ulte ho gaye: call Sana karegi, main nahi.

questions.question: In reported speech (reported on a later day), 'yesterday' usually changes to:
options: the next day
the previous day
that day
tomorrow
questions.explanation: 'yesterday' matlab bolne wale din se ek din pehle, isliye reported speech mein 'the previous day' banta hai. 'the next day' 'tomorrow' ka badla hua roop hai aur 'that day' 'today' ka. Ye teeno pairs aksar mix ho jaate hain.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: Neha said, 'My brother is a pilot.'
options: Neha said that her brother was a pilot.
Neha said that my brother was a pilot.
Neha told that her brother was a pilot.
Neha said that her brother is being a pilot.
questions.explanation: 'My' Neha ke liye hai, toh 'her' banega, aur 'is' → 'was'. 'my brother' mein pronoun nahi badla, jisse lagta hai ki brother report karne wale ka hai. 'told' ke baad person missing hai, aur 'is being' wala continuous form galat hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: The coach said to the players, 'Don't be late.'
options: The coach told the players don't be late.
The coach said the players not to be late.
The coach told the players that not be late.
The coach told the players not to be late.
questions.explanation: Negative command report karne ke liye: told + person + not to + V1. Isliye 'told the players not to be late'. 'don't' direct speech ka form hai jo reported speech mein nahi rehta, 'said the players' mein 'said' ke baad seedha person galat hai, aur 'that not be' grammatical nahi hai.

questions.question: At a mall, a guard said to you, 'You cannot park here.' Later, at home, you report it. Which version is correct?
options: The guard said that I could not park here.
The guard told that I could not park there.
The guard said that I could not park there.
The guard said that he could not park there.
questions.explanation: Ab aap ghar par ho, toh 'here' (mall) → 'there'. 'cannot' → 'could not' aur 'You' (aap) → 'I'. 'park here' ka matlab ab aapka ghar ho jaayega, isliye galat hai. 'told' ke baad person missing hai, aur 'he' likhne se lagta hai ki guard khud park nahi kar sakta.

questions.question: Which direct speech matches this reported speech: 'Meena asked me whether I had finished the report the previous day.'?
options: Meena asked me, 'Will you finish the report tomorrow?'
Meena asked me, 'Did you finish the report yesterday?'
Meena asked me, 'Did I finish the report yesterday?'
Meena asked me, 'Do you finish the report today?'
questions.explanation: Ulta chalo: 'whether' batata hai ki yes/no question tha. 'had finished' ek step aage jaakar 'did finish' banta hai, 'the previous day' → 'yesterday', aur 'I' (main) Meena ke liye 'you' tha: 'Did you finish the report yesterday?' 'Will ... tomorrow' report hota 'would finish the next day', 'Do you ... today' report hota 'finished ... that day', aur 'Did I' mein pronoun galat hai.

questions.question: A week later, you report what Arjun said: 'I can't come now because my mother is ill.' Which version is correct?
options: Arjun said that he couldn't come now because his mother was ill.
Arjun said that I couldn't come then because my mother was ill.
Arjun told that he couldn't come then because his mother was ill.
Arjun said that he couldn't come then because his mother was ill.
questions.explanation: Chaar cheezein badalni hain: 'can't' → 'couldn't', 'is' → 'was', 'I/my' → 'he/his', aur 'now' → 'then' (ek hafte baad 'now' galat time batayega). Pehle option mein 'now' reh gaya, ye sabse bada trap hai. Doosre mein pronouns nahi badle, aur teesre mein 'told' ke baad person missing hai.

questions.question: You have moved to another city. You report what an officer asked you earlier: 'How long have you lived in this city?' Which version is correct?
options: The officer asked me how long had I lived in that city.
The officer asked me how long I have lived in this city.
The officer asked me how long I had lived in that city.
The officer asked me that how long I had lived in that city.
questions.explanation: Wh-question mein wh-word 'how long' rehta hai, word order statement jaisa hota hai ('I had lived'), 'have lived' → 'had lived', aur ab aap doosre sheher mein ho toh 'this city' → 'that city'. Pehle option mein question wala order hai, doosre mein tense aur 'this' nahi badle, aur aakhri mein wh-word ke saath extra 'that' hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: She said, 'I'm hungry. Is there any food?'
options: She said that she was hungry and asked if there was any food.
She said that she was hungry and asked is there any food.
She said that she was hungry and asked if was there any food.
She said that she was hungry and said if there was any food.
questions.explanation: Do parts hain: statement ke liye 'said that she was hungry', aur yes/no question ke liye 'asked if there was any food' (statement order: 'there was'). Doosre option mein question form 'is there' reh gaya, teesre mein 'if' ke baad bhi order ulta hai, aur chauthe mein question ke liye 'said' lagaya, jabki question ke liye 'asked' chahiye.

weeks.title: Conditionals
weeks.summary: Is week aap zero, first, second, third aur mixed conditionals seekhoge, taaki facts, real possibilities, imaginary situations aur past regrets ko sahi tense mein bol sako.
concepts: **Zero conditional**: hamesha sach hone wali baatein. If + present, present. 'If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.'
**First conditional**: future ki real possibility. If + present, will + V1. 'If it rains, we will stay inside.' If-clause mein 'will' nahi aata.
**Second conditional**: abhi ya future ki imaginary/unlikely situation. If + past, would + V1. 'If I had a car, I would drive to college.' Formal English mein 'If I were', 'If I was' nahi.
**Third conditional**: past ki situation jo hui nahi, aksar regret. If + had + V3, would have + V3. 'If I had left earlier, I would have caught the bus.'
**Mixed conditional**: past condition ka present result. If + had + V3, would + V1 (+ now). 'If I had saved money, I would be relaxed now.'
**Unless** = if not. 'Unless you hurry, you will be late' = 'If you do not hurry, you will be late.' Unless ke saath dobara 'not' mat lagao.
**Inversion (formal)**: 'if' hata kar 'had/were/should' ko aage le aao. 'Had I known, I would have called' = 'If I had known...'.

example.problem: Sahi form bhariye (asal mein wo late nikli aur train chhoot gayi): 'If she ___ (leave) earlier, she ___ (catch) the train.'
steps: Situation past ki hai aur jo hua uska ulta soch rahe hain, toh ye third conditional hai.
If-clause mein 'had + V3': 'had left'.
Main clause mein 'would have + V3': 'would have caught'.
Check karo ki if-clause mein 'would' nahi aaya.
Answer: **If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train.**

mistakes: If-clause mein 'will' lagana: 'If it will rain, ...' galat. Sahi: 'If it rains, ...'.
If-clause mein 'would have' lagana: 'If I would have known' galat. Sahi: 'If I had known'.
'Unless' ke saath 'not' bhi lagana: 'Unless you do not study' ka matlab ulta ho jaata hai.
revision: Zero: present + present (facts).
First: present + will + V1 (real future).
Second: past + would + V1 (imaginary, 'If I were').
Third: had + V3 + would have + V3 (past, not real).
Mixed: had + V3 + would + V1 now.
Unless = if not; if-clause mein will/would nahi.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If you heat ice, it ___.'
options: would melt
will have melted
melted
melts
questions.explanation: Ye hamesha sach hone wala fact hai, toh zero conditional: present + present, 'it melts'. 'would melt' second conditional hai jo imaginary situation ke liye hota hai.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.'
options: would cancel
will cancel
cancelled
had cancelled
questions.explanation: Kal baarish hona real possibility hai, toh first conditional: If + present, will + V1. 'would cancel' tab aata jab if-clause past mein hota ('If it rained').

questions.question: Complete the sentence in formal English: 'If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.'
options: am
will be
were
had
questions.explanation: Main tum nahi ho sakta, ye imaginary situation hai, toh second conditional. Formal English mein har subject ke saath 'were' aata hai: 'If I were you'. 'am' aur 'will be' real situation dikhate hain.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If he had checked the address, he ___ lost.'
options: would not have got
will not get
would not get
had not got
questions.explanation: If-clause 'had checked' past perfect hai, aur baat past ki hai, toh third conditional: would have + V3, yaani 'would not have got lost'. 'would not get' second conditional ka pattern hai jo yahan match nahi karta.

questions.question: Which sentence has the same meaning as: 'If you do not apply before Friday, you will lose the seat.'
options: Unless you do not apply before Friday, you will lose the seat.
If you apply before Friday, you will lose the seat.
Unless you apply before Friday, you will lose the seat.
Unless you will apply before Friday, you lose the seat.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' khud 'if not' hai, isliye 'Unless you apply' = 'If you do not apply'. Option A mein double negative se meaning ulta ho gaya, option B ka meaning bilkul alag hai, aur option D mein unless-clause mein 'will' galat hai.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If I had taken the job in Bengaluru last year, I ___ there now.'
options: would have lived
will live
had lived
would be living
questions.explanation: Condition past ki hai ('last year') par result abhi ka hai ('now'), toh mixed conditional: would + V1 (yahan continuous: 'would be living'). Trap option A hai: 'would have lived' past result batata hai jo 'now' se match nahi karta.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If I ___ more time, I would learn the guitar.'
options: have
will have
would have
had
questions.explanation: Main clause mein 'would learn' hai, toh ye second conditional hai: If + past, would + V1. Isliye 'had'. 'have' first conditional ka form hai, aur 'will have' ya 'would have' if-clause mein nahi aate.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If the bus ___ late, I will take an auto.'
options: will be
is
would be
had been
questions.explanation: Main clause mein 'will take' hai, toh first conditional: If + present, will + V1. If-clause mein 'will' nahi aata, isliye 'is' sahi hai, 'will be' nahi. 'would be' aur 'had been' doosre conditionals ke forms hain.

questions.question: Identify the type of conditional: 'If they had invited me, I would have gone.'
options: Zero conditional
First conditional
Third conditional
Second conditional
questions.explanation: If-clause mein 'had + V3' (had invited) aur main clause mein 'would have + V3' (would have gone) hai. Ye third conditional ka pattern hai: past ki baat jo hui nahi (unhone invite nahi kiya tha). Second conditional hota toh 'If they invited me, I would go' hota.

questions.question: Which sentence means the same as: 'If I had known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.'?
options: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
Have I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
Did I know about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
If I would have known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
questions.explanation: Formal inversion mein 'if' hata kar 'had' ko subject se pehle laate hain: 'Had I known...'. 'Have I' aur 'Did I' se third conditional ka 'had + V3' wala pattern toot jaata hai. 'If I would have known' common mistake hai: if-clause mein 'would have' nahi aata.

questions.question: Riya does not have a passport, and the conference is tomorrow, so she cannot go. Complete: 'If Riya ___ a passport, she ___ to the conference in Singapore.'
options: has / will go
had / would go
had had / would have gone
would have / would go
questions.explanation: Abhi ki situation imaginary hai (passport hai hi nahi), toh second conditional: If + past, would + V1 = 'had / would go'. 'has / will go' real possibility dikhata, jo yahan nahi hai. 'had had / would have gone' past ki baat ke liye hai, aur if-clause mein 'would have' nahi aata.

questions.question: Fact: Aman did not set an alarm, so he missed the exam. Which sentence correctly expresses this?
options: If Aman set an alarm, he would not miss the exam.
If Aman had set an alarm, he would have missed the exam.
If Aman would have set an alarm, he would not have missed the exam.
If Aman had set an alarm, he would not have missed the exam.
questions.explanation: Baat past ki hai aur jo hua uska ulta soch rahe hain, toh third conditional: had + V3, would have + V3. Alarm nahi lagaya → exam miss hua, toh ulti situation: alarm lagata → exam miss nahi hota: 'would not have missed'. 'would have missed' wale option ka meaning ulta hai, 'set ... would not miss' second conditional hai (abhi/future ke liye), aur if-clause mein 'would have' galat hai.

questions.question: Fact: Kiran did not take her medicine yesterday, so she is still ill today. Which sentence correctly expresses this?
options: If Kiran had taken her medicine yesterday, she would not be ill today.
If Kiran took her medicine yesterday, she will not be ill today.
If Kiran takes her medicine yesterday, she would not be ill today.
If Kiran had taken her medicine yesterday, she will not be ill today.
questions.explanation: Condition past ki hai ('yesterday') par result abhi ka hai ('today'), aur dono asli situation ke ulte hain, toh mixed conditional: If + had + V3, would + V1 = 'had taken ... would not be ill today'. 'took ... will' aisa lagta hai jaise pata hi na ho ki dawai li ya nahi, jabki fact pata hai. 'had taken ... will' mein imaginary past ke saath real future 'will' fit nahi hota, aur 'takes ... yesterday' mein tense hi galat hai.

questions.question: 'If Neha had not missed the train, she would not have been late for the interview.' What actually happened?
options: She caught the train and was on time.
She missed the train but was on time.
She missed the train and was late.
She caught the train but was late.
questions.explanation: Third conditional hamesha past ki ulti situation batata hai. 'had not missed' ka ulta = usne train miss ki. 'would not have been late' ka ulta = wo late hui. Isliye: train miss hui aur wo late hui. 'caught the train and was on time' sentence ki imaginary situation hai, asli nahi, aur baaki do options mein sirf ek half ulta kiya gaya hai.

questions.question: Which sentence shows that the speaker thinks winning is UNLIKELY?
options: If our team wins tomorrow, we will celebrate.
If our team wins, we celebrate.
If our team had won yesterday, we would have celebrated.
If our team won tomorrow, we would celebrate.
questions.explanation: Future ki unlikely ya imaginary situation ke liye second conditional: If + past, would + V1. 'won tomorrow' mein past form future ke liye use hua hai, jo dikhata hai ki speaker ko jeet ki ummeed kam hai. 'wins tomorrow ... will' real possibility hai, 'wins ... celebrate' general habit hai, aur 'had won yesterday' past ki baat hai, future ki nahi.

weeks.title: Modals
weeks.summary: Is week aap can, could, may, might, must, should, need jaise modals ka sahi use seekhoge: ability, permission, obligation, advice aur logical deduction ke liye.
concepts: **Modal + base verb (V1)**: modal ke baad hamesha V1 aata hai, 'to' nahi aur -s nahi. 'She can swim', 'She can swims' ya 'must to go' galat.
**Ability**: can (present), could (past), be able to (dusre tenses). 'I could read at four.'
**Permission**: may (sabse formal), can (informal), could (polite). 'May I leave early today?'
**Possibility**: may, might, could. 'It might rain later.' Might thoda kam certain hai.
**Obligation**: must (speaker ya authority ka zor), have to (bahar ke rules). **mustn't** = mana hai (prohibition), **needn't / don't have to** = zarurat nahi.
**Advice**: should, ought to. 'You should revise daily.' Past regret: should have + V3: 'I should have started earlier.'
**Deduction (logical guess)**: must be = pakka lagta hai, can't be = bilkul nahi ho sakta. Past ke liye **must have + V3**: 'He must have missed the bus.'
**Polite requests**: Could you / Would you... 'Could you share the slides, please?'

example.problem: Sahi modal chuniye: 'The lights are off and nobody is answering the door. They ___ be out.'
steps: Yahan koi rule ya advice nahi, hum evidence se andaaza laga rahe hain, yaani deduction.
Evidence strong hai (lights off, koi jawab nahi), toh confident guess chahiye.
Confident positive deduction ke liye 'must be' use hota hai.
'should' advice deta, 'can't' ulta matlab deta.
Answer: **They must be out.**

mistakes: Modal ke baad 'to' ya V-ing lagana: 'must to submit', 'can able to' galat. Sahi: 'must submit', 'can' ya 'am able to'.
'mustn't' aur 'don't have to' ko same samajhna: 'You mustn't use phones' = mana hai; 'You don't have to come' = zarurat nahi, aao toh bhi theek.
Past deduction ke liye 'must + V2' likhna: 'He must forgot' galat. Sahi: 'He must have forgotten.'
revision: Modal + V1, beech mein 'to' nahi.
May = formal permission; can = ability ya informal permission.
mustn't = prohibited; needn't = not necessary.
should have + V3 = past advice/regret.
must have + V3 = past deduction.
Could you / Would you = polite request.

questions.question: Choose the most formal way to ask permission: '___ I come in, sir?'
options: Must
May
Shall have
Ought
questions.explanation: Formal permission ke liye 'May' sabse sahi hai: 'May I come in, sir?' 'Must' obligation dikhata hai, aur 'Shall have' aur 'Ought' yahan grammatically fit nahi hote.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence to show ability: 'She ___ speak four languages.'
options: can
must to
ought
may to
questions.explanation: Ability ke liye 'can' + V1: 'She can speak four languages.' 'must to' aur 'may to' mein modal ke baad 'to' galat hai, aur 'ought' ke baad 'to' chahiye tha, saath hi wo ability nahi advice batata hai.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'You ___ bring lunch tomorrow; food will be provided at the workshop.'
options: mustn't
can't
shouldn't to
needn't
questions.explanation: Khaana mil raha hai, toh lunch laane ki zarurat nahi: 'needn't'. 'mustn't' aur 'can't' ka matlab hota ki lunch laana mana hai, jo context se match nahi karta. 'shouldn't to' grammatically galat hai.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'He has been working for 14 hours straight. He ___ be exhausted.'
options: can't
needn't
must
shall
questions.explanation: 14 ghante kaam karne ka strong evidence hai, toh confident deduction: 'must be exhausted'. 'can't be' ulta matlab deta (thaka ho hi nahi sakta), jo logic ke khilaaf hai.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'You ___ told me earlier; I could have helped you.'
options: must have
should have
can have
would
questions.explanation: Speaker past ke baare mein regret/advice de raha hai ki tumhe pehle batana chahiye tha: 'should have told'. 'must have told' ka matlab hota 'pakka bataya hoga', jo deduction hai, advice nahi.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses a logical deduction about the past?
options: She must have left already; her bag isn't here.
She must leave now to catch the train.
She had to leave early yesterday for a meeting.
She should leave before it gets dark.
questions.explanation: 'must have left' + evidence ('bag isn't here') = past ke baare mein logical guess. Trap option C hai: 'had to leave' past mein hai par wo obligation batata hai (jaana pada), guess nahi. Option B present obligation hai aur option D advice.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'You ___ use your phone during the exam; it is against the rules.'
options: needn't
don't have to
mustn't
might
questions.explanation: 'against the rules' matlab mana hai, yaani prohibition, isliye 'mustn't'. 'needn't' aur 'don't have to' ka matlab hota 'zarurat nahi', yaani phone use karna optional hai, jo rule ke ulta hai. 'might' sirf possibility batata hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He can drives a bus to the station.
He should finish the work today.
He must to finish the work.
He cans finish the work.
questions.explanation: Modal ke baad hamesha V1 aata hai, bina 'to' aur bina -s: 'should finish'. 'can drives' mein verb par -s laga hai, 'must to' mein extra 'to' hai, aur modal par khud bhi -s nahi lagta ('cans').

questions.question: Choose the best modal for advice: 'You look tired. You ___ take a short break.'
options: should
mustn't
needn't
can't
questions.explanation: Advice dene ke liye 'should' use hota hai: 'You should take a short break.' 'mustn't' aur 'can't' break lene ko mana kar dete, aur 'needn't' kehta ki break ki zarurat nahi, jo 'You look tired' se match nahi karta.

questions.question: 'Students don't have to wear a uniform on Saturdays.' What does this mean?
options: Wearing a uniform is not allowed on Saturdays.
Students must wear a uniform on Saturdays.
Students should wear a uniform on Saturdays.
Wearing a uniform is not necessary on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: 'don't have to' = zarurat nahi; pehno toh bhi theek, na pehno toh bhi theek. Sabse bada trap 'not allowed' hai: wo 'mustn't' ka matlab hai, 'don't have to' ka nahi. Baaki do options obligation aur advice batate hain.

questions.question: Which sentence shows that the speaker is LEAST certain?
options: He might be at home by now.
He must be at home by now.
He can't be at home yet.
He is definitely at home by now.
questions.explanation: 'might' sirf possibility batata hai, pakka andaaza nahi, isliye sabse kam certain hai. 'must be' confident positive guess hai, 'can't be' confident negative guess hai, aur 'definitely' poori certainty. Trap 'can't be' hai: ye negative hai, par speaker ko pakka yakeen hai.

questions.question: The ground is completely dry this morning, and the roads are dusty. It ___ last night. (Hint: for a guess about the past, put have + V3 after the modal.)
options: must have rained
should have rained
can't have rained
must rain
questions.explanation: Evidence (sookhi zameen, dhool) se past ke baare mein confident negative deduction chahiye. Present mein 'can't be' = bilkul nahi ho sakta; jaise 'must be' past mein 'must have + V3' banta hai, waise hi 'can't' past mein 'can't have + V3' banta hai: 'can't have rained'. 'must have rained' ulta matlab deta hai (pakka baarish hui). 'should have rained' expectation ya regret batata hai, deduction nahi, aur 'must rain' mein past ka sense hi nahi hai.

questions.question: In which sentence does 'could' make a polite request?
options: I could ride a cycle when I was 6.
It could rain later tonight.
We could not find the exam hall.
Could you send me the notes, please?
questions.explanation: 'Could you ..., please?' polite request ka pattern hai. 'I could ride ... when I was 6' past ability hai, 'It could rain' possibility hai, aur 'could not find' past mein ability ki kami hai. Har sentence mein 'could' hai, isliye uska kaam (function) dekh kar decide karna padta hai.

questions.question: Complete: 'The meeting has been cancelled, so you ___ come to the office tomorrow. But you ___ forget to submit the report online by 5 pm; the deadline is strict.'
options: needn't / mustn't
mustn't / needn't
mustn't / mustn't
needn't / needn't
questions.explanation: Meeting cancel ho gayi, toh office aane ki zarurat nahi: 'needn't come'. Deadline strict hai, toh report bhoolna mana hai: 'mustn't forget'. Ulta pair sabse bada trap hai: 'mustn't come' ka matlab hota ki office aana mana hai, aur 'needn't forget' ka koi sense nahi banta.

questions.question: Complete: 'Last year I ___ only run 2 km, but after this training I ___ run 10 km next month.'
options: can / will can
could / will be able to
could / can be able to
was able / will able to
questions.explanation: Past ability ke liye 'could': 'Last year I could only run 2 km'. 'can' ka koi future form nahi hota, isliye future ability ke liye 'will be able to' lagta hai. 'will can' mein do modals saath aa gaye, 'can be able to' ability ko do baar keh deta hai, aur 'was able' / 'will able' mein 'to' aur 'be' missing hain.

weeks.title: Intonation and connected speech
weeks.summary: Is week aap word stress, sentence stress, rising aur falling intonation, aur fluent speech mein hone wale linking, elision aur weak forms ko pehchanna aur bolna seekhoge.
concepts: **Word stress**: lambe word mein ek syllable zyada zor se bola jaata hai. PHO-to-graph, pho-TOG-ra-phy, pho-to-GRAPH-ic. Galat stress se word samajh nahi aata.
**Sentence stress**: content words (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs) par zor, function words (a, the, to, of, and) halke. Isse English ka natural rhythm banta hai.
**Falling intonation**: statements, wh-questions aur commands mein awaaz end mein neeche jaati hai. 'Where do you work?' (fall).
**Rising intonation**: yes/no questions, surprise ya doubt mein awaaz upar jaati hai. 'Are you ready?' (rise).
**Weak forms**: function words ka vowel aksar schwa /ə/ ban jaata hai. 'a cup of tea' mein 'of' /əv/ jaisa bola jaata hai.
**Linking**: word ka last consonant agle word ke vowel se jud jaata hai: 'turn off' sunai deta hai 'tur-noff'.
**Elision aur assimilation**: Elision = koi sound drop ho jaana ('last night' → 'las night'). Assimilation = sound agle sound jaisa ban jaana ('ten boys' → 'tem boys').
**Tag questions**: falling tone = speaker ko yakeen hai, sirf agreement chahiye. Rising tone = sach mein pooch raha hai.

example.problem: Ye sentence do situations mein kaise bolenge? 'You've submitted the report, haven't you?' (a) Aapko pakka pata hai. (b) Aapko sach mein doubt hai.
steps: Main part 'You've submitted the report' statement hai, toh 'report' par halka fall.
Situation (a): aap sirf confirmation chahte ho, toh tag 'haven't you' par **falling** tone.
Situation (b): aap genuinely pooch rahe ho, toh tag 'haven't you' par **rising** tone.
Stress content words par rakho: sub-MIT-ted, RE-port nahi balki re-PORT.
Answer: (a) tag par falling tone = confirm kar rahe ho; (b) tag par rising tone = asli sawaal hai.

mistakes: Har word ko barabar zor se bolna (har syllable same weight). Isse speech robotic lagti hai. Content words par stress do, function words halke rakho.
Wh-questions ko end mein upar le jaana: 'What is your name?' mein normally falling tone hota hai.
Weak forms ko 'galat' samajh kar har 'to', 'of' ko poora bolna. Natural speech mein ye halke hi bole jaate hain.
revision: Content words stressed, function words weak.
Wh-questions aur statements: falling tone.
Yes/no questions: rising tone.
Linking = consonant + vowel jud jaate hain.
Elision = sound drop; assimilation = sound badal jaana.
Tag par fall = yakeen; rise = asli sawaal.

questions.question: Which intonation is normally used at the end of a wh-question like 'Where do you work?'
options: Rising
Level
Falling
No intonation
questions.explanation: Wh-questions (what, where, why, how) mein normally awaaz end mein neeche aati hai, yaani falling tone. Rising tone yes/no questions ka pattern hai, isliye wo common trap hai.

questions.question: A yes/no question like 'Are you ready?' normally ends with:
options: a falling tone
a level tone
no stress at all
a rising tone
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions mein awaaz end mein upar jaati hai, yaani rising tone, jisse listener ko pata chalta hai ki jawab 'yes' ya 'no' chahiye. Falling tone yahan statement jaisa lagta.

questions.question: In the word 'photography', which syllable carries the primary stress?
options: the second syllable (pho-TOG-ra-phy)
the first syllable (PHO-to-gra-phy)
the third syllable (pho-to-GRA-phy)
the last syllable (pho-to-gra-PHY)
questions.explanation: '-graphy' wale words mein stress aksar usse pehle wale syllable par hota hai: pho-TOG-ra-phy. Trap option B hai kyunki 'PHO-to-graph' mein stress pehle syllable par hota hai, par 'photography' mein shift ho jaata hai.

questions.question: In fluent speech, 'last night' often sounds like 'las night'. This process is called:
options: assimilation
elision
linking
intonation
questions.explanation: Yahan /t/ sound bilkul drop ho gaya, aur sound drop hona elision kehlata hai. Assimilation mein sound gayab nahi hota, badal jaata hai (jaise 'ten boys' → 'tem boys').

questions.question: In the sentence 'I want to buy a cup of tea', which words are most likely to be said in their weak forms?
options: want, buy, cup
buy, cup, tea
I, want, tea
to, a, of
questions.explanation: Weak forms function words ke hote hain: 'to', 'a', 'of' (schwa /ə/ ke saath). 'want', 'buy', 'cup', 'tea' content words hain jo meaning carry karte hain, isliye stressed rehte hain.

questions.question: A speaker says 'It's a holiday tomorrow, isn't it?' with a falling tone on 'isn't it'. What does this most likely suggest?
options: The speaker has no idea and is genuinely asking.
The speaker is angry with the listener.
The speaker is fairly sure and expects agreement.
The speaker is giving an order.
questions.explanation: Tag question par falling tone ka matlab hai speaker ko lagbhag yakeen hai aur wo bas agreement chahta hai. Agar wo genuinely pooch raha hota, toh tag par rising tone hota. Isme gussa ya order wala koi signal nahi hai.

questions.question: In a normal English sentence, which words usually carry the stress?
options: function words such as articles, prepositions and pronouns
content words such as nouns and main verbs
only the first word of the sentence
every word, with equal force
questions.explanation: Sentence stress content words par hota hai (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs), kyunki wahi meaning carry karte hain. Function words (a, the, of, to) halke bole jaate hain. Har word ko barabar zor dena common mistake hai, jisse speech robotic lagti hai.

questions.question: Which intonation is normally used at the end of a simple statement like 'I live in Chennai.'?
options: Falling
Rising
Level
No intonation
questions.explanation: Statements mein awaaz end mein neeche aati hai, yaani falling tone, jisse pata chalta hai ki baat poori ho gayi. Rising tone yes/no questions ka pattern hai; statement ko rise ke saath bolne se wo sawaal jaisa sunai deta hai.

questions.question: In fluent speech, 'pick it up' sounds like 'pi-ki-tup'. This process is called:
options: elision
assimilation
linking
a falling tone
questions.explanation: Har word ka last consonant agle word ke vowel se jud gaya: 'pick' ka /k/ 'it' se, aur 'it' ka /t/ 'up' se. Consonant + vowel ka judna linking hai. Elision mein sound drop hota hai aur assimilation mein sound badal jaata hai; yahan koi sound drop nahi hua, sounds bas agle word se jud gaye.

questions.question: In which sentence is 'present' stressed on the second syllable (pre-SENT)?
options: She gave me a lovely present.
All the students were present.
Live in the present, not the past.
I will present my project tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Jab 'present' verb hota hai (kuch dikhana ya pesh karna), stress doosre syllable par aata hai: pre-SENT. Noun ('a lovely present', 'the present') aur adjective ('were present') mein stress pehle syllable par hota hai: PRES-ent. Sirf 'will present my project' mein ye verb hai.

questions.question: In fast speech, 'good boy' often sounds like 'goob boy'. This is an example of:
options: elision
assimilation
linking
a weak form
questions.explanation: /d/ sound agle word ke /b/ jaisa ban gaya, yaani ek sound agle sound jaisa badal gaya; ye assimilation hai (jaise 'ten boys' → 'tem boys'). Elision mein /d/ poora gayab ho jaata, par yahan wo gayab nahi hua, /b/ ban gaya.

questions.question: In the sentence 'I sent the report to my manager on Monday', which words are most likely to be stressed?
options: I, the, to, my
sent, report, manager, Monday
the, report, on, Monday
I, sent, my, on
questions.explanation: Stress content words par aata hai: main verb 'sent' aur nouns 'report', 'manager', 'Monday'. 'I', 'the', 'to', 'my', 'on' function words hain jo halke (aksar weak forms mein) bole jaate hain. Baaki har option mein kam se kam ek function word stressed set mein aa gaya hai.

questions.question: What is the usual tone at the end of each sentence? (i) 'Where did you park?' (ii) 'Did you park outside?' (iii) 'I parked outside.'
options: (i) falling, (ii) rising, (iii) falling
(i) rising, (ii) rising, (iii) falling
(i) falling, (ii) falling, (iii) rising
(i) rising, (ii) falling, (iii) falling
questions.explanation: (i) wh-question hai ('Where'), toh falling. (ii) yes/no question hai ('Did you...?'), toh rising. (iii) statement hai, toh falling. Common trap hai har question ko rising maan lena, jisse 'rising, rising, falling' wala option chuna jaata hai; wh-questions normally fall karte hain.

questions.question: In fluent speech, (i) 'next week' sounds like 'nex week', and (ii) 'an apple' sounds like 'a-napple'. Which processes are these?
options: (i) assimilation, (ii) linking
(i) linking, (ii) elision
(i) elision, (ii) assimilation
(i) elision, (ii) linking
questions.explanation: (i) mein /t/ sound poori tarah drop ho gaya, toh elision ('last night' → 'las night' jaisa). (ii) mein 'an' ka /n/ 'apple' ke vowel se jud gaya, toh linking. Trap (i) ko assimilation kehna hai: assimilation mein sound badalta hai, gayab nahi hota.

questions.question: Which option shows the correct primary stress in BOTH 'economy' and 'economic'?
options: economy: first syllable (E-con-o-my); economic: first syllable (E-co-nom-ic)
economy: second syllable (e-CON-o-my); economic: second syllable (e-CO-nom-ic)
economy: second syllable (e-CON-o-my); economic: third syllable (e-co-NOM-ic)
economy: third syllable (e-con-O-my); economic: third syllable (e-co-NOM-ic)
questions.explanation: 'economy' mein stress doosre syllable par hai: e-CON-o-my. '-ic' wale words mein stress usually '-ic' se theek pehle wale syllable par aata hai, toh 'economic' mein teesre syllable par: e-co-NOM-ic (jaise pho-to-GRAPH-ic). Trap 'second syllable' dono ke liye chunna hai, jo maan leta hai ki word family mein stress ek hi jagah rehta hai; asal mein stress shift hota hai.

weeks.title: Listening for main ideas
weeks.summary: Is week aap kisi lecture ya announcement se main idea (gist) aur specific details nikalna, signpost words pakadna aur smart notes lena seekhoge.
concepts: **Gist / main idea**: poori baat ka central message. Har word samajhna zaroori nahi, overall point pakdo.
**Specific details**: numbers, dates, names, places. Inke liye pehle se pata rakho ki kya sunna hai, phir focus karo.
**Signpost words**: speaker ka direction batate hain. 'Firstly' (list), 'However' (contrast), 'For example' (example), 'To sum up' (conclusion).
**Self-correction trap**: speaker kabhi kehta hai 'Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday'. Hamesha corrected wali info lo.
**Note-taking**: keywords aur abbreviations likho (info, govt, approx, arrows), poore sentences nahi. Baad mein expand karo.
**Speaker's attitude**: tone se pata chalta hai speaker positive hai, doubtful hai ya critical. 'certainly... but' jaise words mixed attitude dikhate hain.
**Predict before listening**: topic aur questions dekh kar andaaza lagao kya aane wala hai, isse sunna aasaan hota hai.

example.problem: Ye announcement padhiye (maan lijiye aapne suna): 'Good morning, everyone. A quick change this week: the library will close at 6 pm instead of 8 pm because of maintenance work. You can still return books at the drop box near Gate 2. Normal timings resume on Monday.' Main idea kya hai, aur library kitne baje band hogi?
steps: Pehle gist: announcement ka purpose kya hai? Library timing mein temporary badlaav.
Signpost 'A quick change' batata hai ki main info aane wali hai.
Detail ke liye number dhoondho: '6 pm instead of 8 pm'. 'instead of' ke baad wala purana time hai, naya time 6 pm hai.
Extra details: reason = maintenance, books = drop box near Gate 2, normal timing = Monday se.
Answer: Main idea: **is week library jaldi band hogi (temporary change)**. Closing time: **6 pm**.

mistakes: Har word likhne ki koshish karna. Isse aage ki baat chhoot jaati hai. Sirf keywords aur numbers likho.
'instead of' ya 'sorry, I mean' ke baad wali correction miss kar dena aur pehla number likh lena.
revision: Gist = overall message; details = numbers, names, dates.
Signposts: firstly, however, for example, to sum up.
Self-correction ke baad wali info final hai.
Notes: keywords + abbreviations.
Tone se speaker ka attitude samjho.

questions.question: When you listen for the 'gist', you are trying to understand:
options: the overall main idea
every number and date
the speaker's accent
the exact words of each sentence
questions.explanation: Gist ka matlab hai overall message ya main idea. Numbers aur dates 'specific details' hain, jo alag listening skill hai. Har word pakadna gist listening ka goal nahi hai.

questions.question: Which phrase signals that the speaker is about to conclude?
options: For instance,
To sum up,
On the other hand,
Firstly,
questions.explanation: 'To sum up' conclusion ka signpost hai. 'For instance' example deta hai, 'On the other hand' contrast dikhata hai, aur 'Firstly' list ki shuruaat karta hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'The workshop was planned for Thursday at 3 pm. Sorry, let me correct that: it will now be on Friday at the same time, in Room 204.' When is the workshop?
options: Thursday at 3 pm
Friday at 2 pm
Friday at 3 pm
Thursday at 2 pm
questions.explanation: Speaker ne correction kiya: din Friday ho gaya aur 'at the same time' matlab time wahi 3 pm. Trap option A hai jo pehli (purani) info hai. Correction ke baad wali baat hi final hoti hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'Many students think that watching recorded lectures at double speed saves time. In practice, they often have to rewind several times, so the total time can end up being the same. A better habit is to watch once at normal speed and make short notes.' What is the speaker's main point?
options: Recorded lectures should be banned.
Students should always rewind lectures.
Double speed is the best way to save time.
Watching once at normal speed with notes is more effective than rushing.
questions.explanation: Speaker pehle ek common belief batata hai, phir 'In practice' se use challenge karta hai, aur 'A better habit is' se apna main point deta hai. Option C wo belief hai jise speaker galat bata raha hai, isliye wo trap hai.

questions.question: While taking notes during a lecture, the most useful approach is to:
options: write keywords and abbreviations, then expand them later
write down every sentence word for word
stop listening whenever you write
note only the examples and skip the main points
questions.explanation: Keywords aur abbreviations likhne se aap sunte bhi reh sakte ho aur baad mein notes expand kar sakte ho. Word-for-word likhne mein aage ki baatein chhoot jaati hain, aur sirf examples likhne se main idea hi gayab ho jaata hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'Well, the new attendance app is certainly faster than the old register. Whether it is accurate is another question. I have already seen three students marked present who were not even on campus.' The speaker's attitude towards the app is best described as:
options: fully enthusiastic
partly positive but doubtful
completely uninterested
angry and hostile
questions.explanation: 'certainly faster' positive hai, par 'Whether it is accurate is another question' aur galat attendance ka example doubt dikhata hai. Isliye attitude mixed hai: partly positive, partly doubtful. 'fully enthusiastic' sirf pehla half dekh kar chuna jaata hai, wo trap hai.

questions.question: Which signpost tells you that the speaker is about to give a contrasting point?
options: For example,
Firstly,
However,
To sum up,
questions.explanation: 'However' contrast ka signpost hai: ab pichhli baat se alag ya ulta point aane wala hai. 'For example' example deta hai, 'Firstly' list shuru karta hai, aur 'To sum up' conclusion batata hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'The bus to the stadium leaves from Stop 4 at 7:15, and the return bus leaves at 10:30.' What time does the return bus leave?
questions.explanation: Sawaal return bus ka hai, toh 'return bus' ke saath wala time sunna hai: 10:30. 7:15 jaane wali bus ka time hai, aur 4 stop number hai, time nahi. Pehle se pata ho ki kaunsi detail chahiye, toh sahi number pakadna aasaan hota hai.

questions.question: Before listening to a talk titled 'Saving water at home', what is the most useful thing to do?
options: Decide to write down every single word you hear
Predict the ideas and words that might come up
Ignore the title so that you stay neutral
Focus only on the speaker's accent and speed
questions.explanation: Title dekh kar andaaza lagana ki kya aane wala hai (taps, leaks, buckets, bills) sunne ko aasaan banata hai. Har word likhne se aage ki baat chhoot jaati hai, aur title ignore karna ek useful clue phenk dena hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'The government will provide approximately 500 new scholarships next year.' Which is the best note?
options: The government will provide approximately 500 new scholarships next year.
scholarships
govt → approx 500 new scholarships next yr
govt → 50 scholarships
questions.explanation: Achhe notes mein keywords, abbreviations aur sahi number hote hain: 'govt', 'approx', '500', 'next yr'. Poora sentence likhna slow hai, sirf 'scholarships' likhne se number aur time chhoot jaate hain, aur '50' galat number hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'Attention, please. Because of heavy rain, today's outdoor sports meet is postponed. Participants should collect their kits from the gym. A new date will be shared by email.' What is the main purpose of this announcement?
options: To say that the sports meet has been postponed
To explain where participants can find the gym
To advertise the new sports kits available in the gym
To announce the new date and venue of the sports meet
questions.explanation: Announcement ka central message hai ki baarish ki wajah se sports meet postpone ho gayi. Gym aur kits extra details hain. Trap 'new date' wala option hai: speaker ne naya date bataya hi nahi, sirf kaha ki wo email se aayega.

questions.question: You hear: 'The fee is ₹1,200 per student. Oh, sorry, that's last year's fee; this year it's ₹1,500. And if you register before Friday, you get ₹200 off.' Pooja registers on Wednesday, 2 days before that Friday. How much does she pay?
questions.explanation: Pehle correction pakdo: ₹1,200 purani fee hai, is saal ki fee ₹1,500 hai. Pooja Friday se pehle (Wednesday) register karti hai, toh ₹200 off: 1,500 − 200 = ₹1,300. ₹1,000 tab aata jab purani fee se discount ghataate (correction miss), aur ₹1,500 mein discount bhool gaye.

questions.question: You hear the start of a talk: 'There are three reasons why I recommend cycling to college. Firstly, it saves money. Secondly, it keeps you fit.' What is the speaker most likely to say next?
options: To sum up, cycling is dangerous.
Thirdly, it reduces traffic and pollution.
However, I would never recommend cycling to anyone.
For example, my uncle drives a car.
questions.explanation: Speaker ne 'three reasons' ka promise kiya aur 'Firstly', 'Secondly' bol chuka hai, toh agla signpost 'Thirdly' hoga, jisme teesra reason aayega. 'To sum up, cycling is dangerous' aur 'I would never recommend cycling' uski apni baat ke ulta hain, aur 'my uncle drives a car' cycling ka example hi nahi hai.

questions.question: You hear: 'From 1 July, our college buses will follow a new route. They will now stop at the metro station, so students from the east side can reach campus in half the time. The fare stays the same, and the new timetable is on the notice board.' Which statement best gives the MAIN idea?
options: The bus fare will stay the same for all students.
The new timetable for the college buses is on the notice board.
From 1 July, a new route will cut many students' travel time.
The metro station near the east side will close on 1 July.
questions.explanation: Main idea poori baat ko cover karta hai: 1 July se naya route, jisse east side ke students ka travel time aadha ho jaayega. Fare aur timetable wale options sach hain, par sirf details hain, isliye trap hain. Metro station band hone ki baat kahi hi nahi gayi.

questions.question: You hear: 'I was sure the workshop would be a waste of a Saturday. To my surprise, it turned out to be the most useful session I've attended this year.' How did the speaker's attitude change?
options: From doubtful to very positive
From positive to disappointed
Positive from beginning to end
Doubtful from beginning to end
questions.explanation: Shuru mein speaker ko lagta tha ki workshop 'waste' hogi (doubtful, negative). 'To my surprise' signal hai ki opinion badal gaya, aur 'most useful session' bahut positive hai. Isliye doubtful se very positive. Sirf pehla sentence sunke 'Doubtful from beginning to end' chunna trap hai.

weeks.title: Reading strategies
weeks.summary: Is week aap skimming, scanning aur inference jaise reading strategies seekhoge, saath hi context se naye words ka meaning nikalna aur fact ko opinion se alag karna.
concepts: **Skimming**: text ko jaldi se padh kar general idea lena. Title, headings, pehla aur aakhri paragraph, aur har paragraph ka pehla sentence dekho.
**Scanning**: kisi ek specific info (date, naam, number) ko dhoondhna. Poora text nahi padhte, sirf us keyword par nazar daudaate ho.
**Topic sentence**: paragraph ka main idea batane wala sentence, aksar paragraph ki shuruaat mein hota hai.
**Inference**: jo seedha nahi likha par evidence se logically samajh aata hai. Inference hamesha text ke clues par based hona chahiye, apni kalpana par nahi.
**Context clues**: anjaan word ka meaning aas-paas ke words se nikaalo. 'so ... that' (result), 'but' (contrast), examples sab clue dete hain.

**Fact vs opinion**: fact check kiya ja sakta hai ('The meeting is at 5 pm'). Opinion personal judgement hai ('The meeting was boring'). Words jaise best, worst, should, beautiful opinion ka signal hain.
**Author's purpose aur tone**: author inform kar raha hai, persuade kar raha hai ya entertain? Tone serious, critical, ya humorous hai?

example.problem: Passage: 'Rohan's tea stall near the bus stand used to close at 9 pm. Last year he installed a solar panel and two LED lights. Now he stays open till midnight, and night-shift drivers have become his most regular customers. He plans to add a second panel before winter.' Kya infer kiya ja sakta hai?
steps: Pehle skim karo: passage Rohan ke tea stall mein aaye badlaav ke baare mein hai.
Clues dekho: solar panel + lights ke baad stall der tak khula rehta hai.
Naye customers (night-shift drivers) mile hain, aur wo doosra panel lagana chahta hai.
Agar business nuksaan mein hota toh wo aur invest nahi karta. Isse lagta hai ki change faydemand raha.
Jo nahi likha (jaise exact income) us par claim mat karo.
Answer: **Solar setup ki wajah se Rohan ka business badha hai, aur wo is change se khush hai.**

mistakes: Inference ke naam par apni kalpana jod dena. Har inference ke liye passage mein clue point kar paana chahiye.
Specific info dhoondhne ke liye poora passage shuru se padhna. Scanning karo: keyword ya number par seedha jaao.
Opinion ko fact maan lena kyunki wo confidence se likha hai.
revision: Skimming = gist; scanning = specific info.
Topic sentence = paragraph ka main idea.
Inference = evidence-based conclusion.
Context clues se anjaan words samjho.
Fact check ho sakta hai; opinion judgement hai.

questions.question: You need to find the exam date in a long notice. Which reading strategy fits best?
options: Skimming
Inferring
Summarising
Scanning
questions.explanation: Ek specific info (date) dhoondhni hai, toh scanning sahi hai. Skimming general idea ke liye hoti hai, isliye wo common confusion hai.

questions.question: Skimming a passage mainly helps you to:
options: memorise all the facts
find one particular phone number
get a quick idea of what the text is about
check spelling mistakes
questions.explanation: Skimming ka goal hai jaldi se overall idea lena. Ek particular phone number dhoondhna scanning hai, aur facts memorise karna ya spelling check karna skimming ka kaam nahi.

questions.question: Passage: 'The hostel mess changed its menu last month. Since then, the queue at the canteen outside the campus has become noticeably shorter.' Which inference is best supported by the passage?
options: The canteen has closed down.
Students seem to prefer the new mess menu.
The mess food has become more expensive.
The canteen staff went on leave.
questions.explanation: 'Since then' menu change aur chhoti queue ko jodta hai, toh lagta hai students ab mess mein zyada kha rahe hain. Canteen band hota toh queue hi nahi hoti, 'shorter' nahi likha jaata. Price ya staff ke baare mein passage mein koi clue nahi hai.

questions.question: 'The new policy was so ambiguous that even the managers interpreted it in different ways.' Here, 'ambiguous' most likely means:
options: open to more than one meaning
very strict
extremely old
clearly written
questions.explanation: 'so ... that' result batata hai: managers ne alag-alag meaning nikale. Iska matlab policy ke ek se zyada meaning nikal sakte the. 'clearly written' bilkul ulta hai, aur 'strict' ya 'old' se alag interpretations nahi hote.

questions.question: Which of these is an opinion rather than a fact?
options: A week has seven days.
Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Online degrees are the most enjoyable way to study.
Chennai is a city in Tamil Nadu.
questions.explanation: 'most enjoyable' personal judgement hai, sabke liye check nahi ho sakta, isliye opinion hai. Baaki teeno verify kiye ja sakte hain, toh facts hain.

questions.question: Passage: 'Meera had rehearsed her presentation five times. On the day, however, the projector failed. Without pausing, she picked up a marker and drew her main chart on the whiteboard. A week later, her manager asked her to train the new interns.' Which inference is best supported?
options: Meera dislikes using projectors.
The manager was unhappy with the presentation.
The interns had already seen the presentation.
The manager was impressed by how Meera handled the problem.
questions.explanation: Meera ne bina ruke problem handle ki, aur uske baad manager ne use interns ko train karne ki responsibility di. Ye trust aur appreciation ka sign hai. Projector se nafrat ya interns ke baare mein koi clue nahi hai, aur 'unhappy' evidence ke ulta hai.

questions.question: A good inference about a passage must be based on:
options: your own imagination
the length of the passage
clues given in the text
what you hope will happen next
questions.explanation: Inference wo hai jo seedha nahi likha, par text ke evidence se logically nikalta hai. Har inference ke liye passage mein clue point kar paana chahiye. Apni kalpana ya ummeed jodna common mistake hai, aur passage ki length se meaning nahi nikalta.

questions.question: Which of these is a fact rather than an opinion?
options: The library is the most peaceful place on campus.
The library opens at 8 am on weekdays.
Students should spend more time in the library.
The new library building looks beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'opens at 8 am on weekdays' check kiya ja sakta hai (notice ya timings dekh kar), isliye fact hai. Baaki teeno mein opinion ke signal words hain: 'most peaceful', 'should', 'beautiful', jo personal judgement hain.

questions.question: 'Unlike his talkative sister, Varun is quite reticent in class.' Here, 'reticent' most likely means:
options: very talkative
often late
very intelligent
quiet and reserved
questions.explanation: 'Unlike' contrast ka clue hai: Varun apni talkative sister jaisa nahi hai, yaani wo kam bolta hai. Isliye 'reticent' = quiet and reserved. 'very talkative' ulta hai, aur 'late' ya 'intelligent' ke liye sentence mein koi clue nahi.

questions.question: Passage: 'Join the Green Campus Drive this Sunday! Just 2 hours of your time can help plant 200 trees. Sign up at the student office today; don't miss this chance to make a difference.' What is the author's main purpose?
options: to persuade students to join the drive
to inform readers about the history of trees
to entertain readers with a funny story
to criticise the student office
questions.explanation: 'Join...!', 'Sign up today' aur 'don't miss this chance' jaise words reader ko action lene ke liye push kar rahe hain, toh purpose persuade karna hai. Number (200 trees) information jaisa lagta hai, par wo bhi convince karne ke liye diya gaya hai. Passage mein na koi history hai, na kahani, na criticism.
