questions.question: Which sentence is the topic sentence of this paragraph? 'Public libraries offer far more than books. Many run free computer classes. Some host exam-preparation groups for students. Others organise weekend story sessions for children.'
options: Many run free computer classes.
Public libraries offer far more than books.
Some host exam-preparation groups for students.
Others organise weekend story sessions for children.
questions.explanation: Topic sentence paragraph ka main idea batata hai, aur baaki sentences use support karte hain. 'Public libraries offer far more than books' general idea hai, aur computer classes, exam groups, story sessions uske examples hain. Baaki teeno options sirf supporting details hain.

questions.question: Passage: 'Every morning at 6, Ishaan's light goes on. By the time his roommates wake up, he has already practised on his keyboard for an hour. On his desk lies an entry form for the national music competition, half filled in.' Which inference is best supported?
options: Ishaan will definitely win the national competition.
Ishaan's roommates dislike hearing his music every morning.
Ishaan cannot sleep at night.
Ishaan is preparing to take part in a music competition.
questions.explanation: Clues: roz subah 6 baje ek ghanta practice, aur desk par competition ka aadha bhara entry form. Dono milkar dikhate hain ki wo competition ki taiyari kar raha hai. 'definitely win' evidence se aage ki baat hai (overclaim), aur roommates ki pasand ya neend ki problem ka koi clue nahi.

questions.question: Which sentence contains BOTH a fact and an opinion?
options: The bridge, which opened in 2021, is the ugliest structure in the city.
The bridge, which has 4 lanes, opened to traffic in 2021.
The bridge is ugly, and its design is the worst in the whole city.
The bridge is 2 km long and was the first in the city with a cycle lane.
questions.explanation: 'which opened in 2021' check kiya ja sakta hai (fact), aur 'the ugliest structure in the city' personal judgement hai (opinion). 'which has 4 lanes, opened to traffic in 2021' aur '2 km long ... cycle lane' sirf facts hain, aur 'ugly ... worst in the whole city' sirf opinion hai.

questions.question: 'After weeks of heavy rain, the once barren field was now lush, covered with tall green grass.' Here, 'barren' most likely means:
options: wet and muddy
covered with tall grass
having almost no plants
full of flowers
questions.explanation: 'once ... now' contrast dikhata hai: pehle field barren tha, ab lush (hari ghaas se bhara) hai. Toh barren uska ulta hai: jahan lagbhag kuch nahi ugta. 'covered with tall grass' field ki abhi ki haalat hai, pehle ki nahi, aur 'wet and muddy' sirf 'rain' word dekh kar chuna gaya trap hai.

questions.question: Passage: 'Oh wonderful, another urgent meeting about the printer. That makes three this week. I'm sure this one will finally fix everything.' The writer's tone is best described as:
options: sincerely enthusiastic
grateful and relieved
neutral and factual
critical, using sarcasm
questions.explanation: Words positive hain ('wonderful', 'finally fix everything'), par context ulta hai: printer par is hafte teesri meeting. Jab words kuch aur kahein aur matlab ulta ho, wo sarcasm hai, aur yahan writer meetings ki aalochna (critical) kar raha hai. Sirf words dekh kar 'enthusiastic' chunna trap hai.

weeks.title: Professional vocabulary and idioms
weeks.summary: Is week aap workplace ke liye formal words, sahi collocations, common phrasal verbs aur idioms seekhoge, aur confusing word pairs (affect/effect jaise) ka fark samjhoge.
concepts: **Formal vs informal words**: professional writing mein formal option chuno. get → receive/obtain, ask for → request, help → assist, tell → inform, buy → purchase.
**Collocations**: kuch words hamesha saath aate hain. meet a deadline, make a decision, take responsibility, conduct a survey, raise a concern. 'do a decision' galat lagta hai.
**Phrasal verbs at work**: follow up (dobara contact karke status poochna), look into (investigate karna), carry out (execute karna), put off (postpone karna), call off (cancel karna).

**Idioms**: on the same page (sabki samajh ek jaisi), touch base (thoda contact karna), the ball is in your court (ab tumhari baari decide karne ki), back to square one (phir se shuru), go the extra mile (expected se zyada mehnat).
**Confusable pairs**: affect (verb, asar daalna) vs effect (noun, asar); advice (noun) vs advise (verb); principal (head/main) vs principle (rule); complement (poora karna) vs compliment (tareef).
**Idioms ka sahi jagah use**: formal reports mein idioms kam rakho; meetings aur emails mein halka use theek hai.

example.problem: Is informal message ko formal banaiye: 'Hey, can you get me the numbers ASAP? Boss wants them.'
steps: 'Hey' informal hai: 'Dear Mr. Kumar' ya 'Hello Mr. Kumar' jaise greeting lagao.
'can you get me' → 'Could you please send me' (polite request + formal verb).
'the numbers' → 'the figures' (professional word).
'ASAP' vague aur informal hai: specific time do, jaise 'by 3 pm today'.
'Boss wants them' → 'The manager has requested them for the review meeting.'
Answer: **Could you please send me the figures by 3 pm today? The manager has requested them for the review meeting.**

mistakes: affect aur effect mein confusion: 'The rain effected the match' galat; sahi 'The rain affected the match' (verb) ya 'The rain had an effect on the match' (noun).
Phrasal verb ka galat particle: 'look after the bug' (dekhbhaal karna) vs 'look into the bug' (investigate karna). Particle badalte hi meaning badal jaata hai.
Formal report mein idioms aur slang bharna, jisse tone casual ho jaati hai.
revision: get → receive, ask for → request, help → assist.
meet a deadline, make a decision, take responsibility.
follow up, look into, carry out, put off, call off.
Affect = verb, effect = noun (usually).
Idioms emails/meetings mein theek, reports mein kam.

questions.question: Which is the most formal replacement for 'get' in: 'We will get your documents by Monday'?
options: grab
receive
pick up
catch
questions.explanation: Formal context mein 'get' ki jagah 'receive' best hai: 'We will receive your documents by Monday.' 'grab' aur 'catch' informal hain, aur 'pick up' ka meaning physically uthana ho jaata hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct collocation: 'Our team has to ___ the deadline.'
options: meet
do
finish
reach up
questions.explanation: Standard collocation 'meet a deadline' hai. 'do the deadline' ya 'finish the deadline' natural English nahi hai, kyunki deadline koi kaam nahi, ek time limit hai.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'go the extra mile' mean?
options: travel a long distance for work
refuse to take extra work
walk to the office every day
make more effort than is expected
questions.explanation: 'go the extra mile' ka matlab hai expected se zyada mehnat karna. Idiom ka literal meaning (sach mein mile chalna) nahi lena chahiye, isliye option A trap hai.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The new rule will ___ all employees who joined after 2024.'
options: effect
affection
affect
effective
questions.explanation: Yahan 'will' ke baad verb chahiye jiska matlab 'asar daalna' ho: 'affect'. 'effect' usually noun hai (as a verb uska matlab 'laagu karke laana' hota hai, jo yahan fit nahi). 'affection' aur 'effective' alag parts of speech hain.

questions.question: Your manager says, 'I have shared my comments. The ball is in your court now.' What does she mean?
options: It is now your turn to take a decision or act.
You have won the discussion.
You are responsible for the mistake that happened.
You should play a sport during the break.
questions.explanation: 'The ball is in your court' ka matlab hai ab agla step tumhe lena hai. Manager ne apna kaam kar diya, ab tumhari baari hai. Isme jeet ya galti ka blame wala meaning nahi hai.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the phrasal verb correctly in a professional context?
options: Please look after the error in the code before the release.
I will follow up with the vendor about the delayed shipment.
Please carry on the report by Friday.
The manager called off the employee for being late.
questions.explanation: 'follow up with someone' = status ke liye dobara contact karna, bilkul sahi use hai. Error ke liye 'look into' (investigate) chahiye, 'look after' nahi. 'carry on the report' ka matlab nahi banta, aur 'call off' ka matlab cancel karna hai, daantna nahi.

questions.question: Which word is the most formal replacement for 'help' in: 'Our staff will help you with the registration'?
options: pitch in
assist
lend a hand
chip in
questions.explanation: Professional writing mein 'help' ki jagah formal word 'assist' hai: 'Our staff will assist you with the registration.' Baaki teeno informal phrases hain, aur sentence mein 'you' ke saath seedha fit bhi nahi hote.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'During the meeting, Priya ___ a concern about the budget.'
options: rose
did
raised
lifted
questions.explanation: Collocation 'raise a concern' hai, past mein 'raised a concern'. Trap 'rose' hai: 'rise' ka object nahi hota (prices rose), jabki 'raise' object leta hai (raise a concern, raise a question). 'did a concern' aur 'lifted a concern' natural English nahi hain.

questions.question: 'The match was called off because of rain.' Here, 'called off' means:
options: postponed
started
shortened
cancelled
questions.explanation: 'call off' = cancel karna. Trap 'postponed' hai: wo 'put off' ka matlab hai (kisi baad ki date tak taalna). Dono phrasal verbs milte-julte lagte hain, par cancel aur postpone alag cheezein hain.

questions.question: Before the client meeting, the team leader says, 'Let's have a quick call to make sure we are all on the same page.' What does she want?
options: everyone to share the same understanding
everyone to read the same page of the report
the client meeting to be shorter than usual
someone to take notes during the quick call
questions.explanation: Idiom 'on the same page' ka matlab hai sabki samajh ek jaisi hona. Team leader chahti hai ki meeting se pehle sab plan ko ek jaisa samjhein. Literal meaning (report ka same page padhna) lena trap hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair: 'Her ___ was useful, so I will ___ my juniors in the same way.'
options: advise / advice
advice / advise
advice / advice
advise / advise
questions.explanation: Pehle blank mein 'Her' ke baad noun chahiye: 'advice'. Doosre blank mein 'will' ke baad verb chahiye: 'advise'. Advice (noun) aur advise (verb) ka pronunciation bhi alag hai: /s/ aur /z/. Ulta pair sabse common galti hai.

questions.question: Which sentence has NO vocabulary error?
options: The blue curtains complement the white walls.
The weather had a big affect on attendance.
She complemented me on my presentation.
We must follow this principal in every project.
questions.explanation: 'complement' ka matlab hai poora karna ya saath mein achha lagna, toh blue curtains white walls ko complement karte hain (unke saath achhe lagte hain), ye sahi hai. 'a big affect' mein noun chahiye tha: 'effect'. Tareef ke liye 'complimented' hona chahiye, aur rule ke liye 'principle' aata hai, 'principal' (head) nahi.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair: 'The IT team will look ___ the login problem, and the product launch has been put ___ until next week.'
options: after / off
into / on
after / out
into / off
questions.explanation: Problem ko investigate karna = 'look into'. Launch ko aage taalna (postpone) = 'put off'. 'look after' ka matlab dekhbhaal karna hai, jo bug ke saath galat hai, aur 'put on' / 'put out' ka matlab postpone nahi hota.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The client rejected all three designs, so after two months of work we are ___.'
options: on the same page
going the extra mile
back to square one
touching base
questions.explanation: Teeno designs reject ho gaye, toh team ko phir se shuru karna padega: 'back to square one'. 'on the same page' sahmati batata hai, 'going the extra mile' extra mehnat, aur 'touching base' thoda contact karna; inme se koi bhi 'rejection ke baad shuru se karna' nahi batata.

questions.question: Which sentence uses ALL the collocations correctly?
options: We need to make a decision, take responsibility and meet the deadline.
We need to do a decision, take responsibility and meet the deadline.
We need to make a decision, make responsibility and meet the deadline.
We need to make a decision, take responsibility and do the deadline.
questions.explanation: Sahi collocations: make a decision, take responsibility, meet a deadline. Har galat option mein sirf ek word badla hai: 'do a decision', 'make responsibility', 'do the deadline'. Isliye har phrase ko alag se check karna padta hai; ek hissa sahi dekh kar poora sentence sahi mat maano.

weeks.title: Formal emails and reports
weeks.summary: Is week aap ek formal email ka structure, sahi subject line, greeting aur closing, aur short report ke sections aur objective tone seekhoge.
concepts: **Email structure**: Subject line → Salutation → Opening line (purpose) → Body (details) → Call to action (kya chahiye) → Closing → Signature (naam, roll no./designation).
**Subject line**: chhoti aur specific. 'Request for extension: Week 5 assignment' achhi hai; 'Hi' ya 'Urgent!!!' nahi.
**Salutation aur closing**: naam pata ho toh 'Dear Dr. Sharma' + 'Yours sincerely' ya 'Regards'. Naam na pata ho toh 'Dear Sir or Madam' + 'Yours faithfully' (British convention).
**Tone**: polite, concise, clear. SMS language (pls, u, thx), ALL CAPS, aur bahut saare exclamation marks avoid karo.
**To, CC, BCC**: To = main receiver; CC = jinko info chahiye; BCC = hidden copy, receivers ek doosre ke email ID nahi dekh paate.
**Report structure**: Title → Introduction (purpose) → Method (data kaise liya) → Findings → Conclusion → Recommendations (aage kya karna chahiye).
**Objective language in reports**: facts aur numbers, third person ya passive voice, emotional words nahi. 'The survey found that...' achha hai; 'We were shocked' nahi.

example.problem: Apne course instructor ko assignment deadline extension ke liye ek short formal email likhiye (aap 2 din hospital mein the).
steps: Subject: 'Request for extension: Week 5 assignment'.
Salutation: 'Dear Dr. Iyer,'.
Opening line mein purpose: 'I am writing to request a short extension for the Week 5 assignment.'
Body mein reason aur proof: 'I was admitted to hospital on 10 and 11 March, and I have attached the discharge summary.'
Call to action: 'Could I submit the assignment by 15 March?'
Closing aur signature: 'Thank you for considering my request. Regards, Ankit Verma, Roll No. 42'.
Answer: In sab parts ko isi order mein jodo; email chhota, polite aur ek hi request par focused rahega.

mistakes: Subject line khaali chhodna ya vague likhna. Receiver ko subject dekh kar hi pata chalna chahiye ki email kis baare mein hai.
'Dear Sir or Madam' ke saath 'Yours sincerely' aur naam wale salutation ke saath 'Yours faithfully' mix karna.
Report mein personal feelings likhna ('I feel the canteen is the worst'). Data aur evidence ke saath likho.
revision: Subject → Salutation → Purpose → Details → Action → Closing.
Specific subject line likho.
Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully; Dear + naam → Yours sincerely.
BCC = receivers ki privacy.
Report: Intro, Method, Findings, Conclusion, Recommendations.
Report mein objective, data-based language.

questions.question: Which subject line is most suitable for a formal email?
options: Hi!!
Urgent pls read
Request for extension of Week 5 assignment deadline
Something about assignment
questions.explanation: Achhi subject line specific hoti hai aur batati hai email kis baare mein hai. 'Hi!!' aur 'Urgent pls read' informal aur vague hain, aur 'Something about assignment' se purpose clear nahi hota.

questions.question: In British formal usage, which closing correctly pairs with the salutation 'Dear Sir or Madam'?
options: Yours lovingly
Cheers
Yours sincerely
Yours faithfully
questions.explanation: Jab receiver ka naam nahi pata ('Dear Sir or Madam'), British convention mein 'Yours faithfully' aata hai. 'Yours sincerely' tab use hota hai jab naam se address kiya ho. 'Cheers' aur 'Yours lovingly' formal nahi hain.

questions.question: Which opening line is most appropriate in a formal email to a professor you have never met?
options: I am writing to ask whether I could join your summer research project.
Hey Prof, wanna join your project!
I want to join your project. Reply fast.
As you already know me, please add me to your project.
questions.explanation: Pehli line purpose ko politely aur clearly batati hai: 'I am writing to ask whether...'. Option B slang wala hai, option C rude lagta hai, aur option D galat assume karta hai ki professor aapko jaante hain.

questions.question: In a formal report, which section usually states what should be done next?
options: Introduction
Recommendations
Method
Title
questions.explanation: Recommendations section mein findings ke basis par aage ke steps suggest kiye jaate hain. Introduction purpose batata hai aur Method batata hai data kaise collect hua.

questions.question: Which sentence best suits the objective tone of a report?
options: We were totally shocked by the terrible results!
I personally feel the canteen is the worst on campus.
Everyone obviously hates the new timetable.
The survey found that 62% of respondents preferred online classes.
questions.explanation: Objective tone mein data aur neutral language hoti hai: 'The survey found that 62%...'. Baaki options mein emotional words (shocked, terrible), personal opinion (I personally feel) aur bina proof ki generalisation (Everyone obviously hates) hain.

questions.question: You must send one email to 40 external participants without letting them see each other's email addresses. Where should you put their addresses?
options: To
CC
BCC
Subject
questions.explanation: BCC (blind carbon copy) mein daale gaye addresses doosre receivers ko dikhte nahi, isliye privacy bachti hai. Trap option B hai: CC mein sab addresses sabko dikhte hain, toh privacy toot jaati hai. 'To' ka bhi yahi problem hai.

questions.question: In a formal email that begins 'Dear Dr. Sharma,', which closing is correct?
options: Yours faithfully
Yours sincerely
Love
Bye for now
questions.explanation: Jab receiver ko naam se address karte ho ('Dear Dr. Sharma'), tab 'Yours sincerely' aata hai. 'Yours faithfully' sirf tab jab naam na pata ho ('Dear Sir or Madam'). 'Love' aur 'Bye for now' formal email ke liye nahi hain.

questions.question: You email your project report to your guide. Your team leader should get a copy for information, and the guide should be able to see this. Where should the team leader's address go?
options: To
BCC
Subject
CC
questions.explanation: CC un logon ke liye hai jinko info chahiye, aur CC ke addresses sabko dikhte hain, toh guide ko pata rahega ki team leader ko bhi copy gayi. 'To' main receiver (guide) ke liye hai. BCC mein address chhupa rehta, jo yahan nahi chahiye.

questions.question: Which sentence is suitable for a formal email?
options: Pls send the file asap, thx a lot
PLEASE SEND THE FILE BY TODAY ITSELF!!!
Could you please send the file by 5 pm?
u need to send me the file by 5 pm
questions.explanation: Formal tone polite, clear aur specific hoti hai: 'Could you please ... by 5 pm?'. 'Pls', 'asap', 'thx', 'u' SMS language hai, aur ALL CAPS ke saath exclamation marks chillane jaise lagte hain.

questions.question: Arrange these parts of a formal email in the correct order: (P) Closing, (Q) Salutation, (R) Body with details, (S) Opening line stating the purpose.
options: S, Q, R, P
Q, S, R, P
Q, R, S, P
Q, S, P, R
questions.explanation: Order hai: Salutation (Q) → Opening line jo purpose batati hai (S) → Body (R) → Closing (P). Trap 'S, Q, R, P' hai: purpose wali line salutation ke baad aati hai, pehle nahi. 'Q, R, S, P' mein purpose details ke baad aa gaya, jo reader ko confuse karta hai.

questions.question: Which line is a clear call to action in an email requesting a seminar room?
options: Could you confirm by Thursday if the room is free?
I hope you are doing well and had a good weekend.
I am writing regarding the booking of the seminar room.
Thank you for your time and support.
questions.explanation: Call to action batata hai ki receiver ko kya karna hai aur kab tak: 'confirm by Thursday'. 'I hope you are doing well...' sirf polite opening hai, 'I am writing regarding...' purpose batata hai par koi action nahi maangta, aur 'Thank you for your time...' closing line hai.

questions.question: A report on canteen use has these sentences. Which one belongs in the Findings section?
options: This report examines how students use the campus canteen.
A questionnaire was given to 150 students in March.
Of the 150 students surveyed, 96 eat lunch in the canteen every day.
The canteen should open a second billing counter to reduce lunch queues.
questions.explanation: Findings mein data se nikla result hota hai: '150 mein se 96 students roz lunch canteen mein karte hain'. Pehla sentence Introduction (purpose) hai, doosra Method (data kaise liya), aur 'should open a second billing counter' Recommendation hai. Trap Method wala sentence hai kyunki usme bhi number hai, par wo result nahi, process batata hai.

questions.question: A report draft says: 'Everyone hated the new timetable and it was a total disaster!' The survey shows that 72% of students were dissatisfied with it. Which is the best objective rewrite?
options: Honestly, the new timetable was a total disaster for all of us students.
We were shocked that everyone hated the new timetable.
The new timetable was terrible, as everyone in the college already knows.
The survey found that 72% of students were dissatisfied with the timetable.
questions.explanation: Objective report language mein data aur neutral words hote hain: 'The survey found that 72%...'. Baaki teeno mein emotional words ('disaster', 'shocked', 'terrible') aur bina proof ki generalisation ('everyone', 'all of us') hai. Saath hi 'everyone hated' galat bhi hai, kyunki data 72% batata hai, 100% nahi.

questions.question: Read the email. What is its main weakness?
questions.code:
Subject: Hi

Dear Ms. Rao,

I am writing to request the slides from Monday's guest lecture. I missed the session because I was on duty at the college fest.

Could you please share them by Friday?

Yours sincerely,
Karan Mehta, Roll No. 18
options: The subject line is vague.
The closing does not match the salutation.
There is no call to action.
The purpose is not stated.
questions.explanation: Subject 'Hi' se pata hi nahi chalta ki email kis baare mein hai; 'Request for slides: Monday's guest lecture' jaisi line honi chahiye. Baaki sab theek hai: 'Dear Ms. Rao' ke saath 'Yours sincerely' match karta hai, call to action ('share them by Friday') hai, aur purpose pehli line mein hai.

questions.question: Riya sends an email with To: her manager; CC: 5 team members; BCC: the HR officer. Which statement is TRUE?
options: The team members can see that the HR officer also received a copy.
The manager can see the team's addresses but not the HR officer's.
The HR officer's address is visible to everyone.
The team members cannot see the manager's address in the To field.
questions.explanation: To aur CC ke addresses sab receivers ko dikhte hain, isliye manager team ke addresses dekh sakta hai, aur team manager ka. BCC hidden copy hai, toh HR officer ka address kisi aur ko nahi dikhta. Isliye team ko pata nahi chalta ki HR ko copy gayi, aur 'visible to everyone' galat hai.

weeks.title: Presentations and group discussions
weeks.summary: Is week aap ek clear presentation plan karna, signposting aur slides ka sahi use, aur group discussion mein politely bolna, disagree karna aur summarise karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Presentation structure**: Opening (hook + topic) → Agenda (kya cover karoge) → Body (2-3 main points) → Conclusion (summary) → Q&A.
**Hook**: shuru mein attention pakdo: ek sawaal, ek surprising number, ya chhoti si real situation.
**Signposting in presentations**: 'Let me begin with...', 'Let me now move on to...', 'To summarise...'. Isse audience ko pata rehta hai aap kahan ho.
**Slides**: clear heading, kam text, bade fonts, ek slide par ek idea. Slides support hain, script nahi.
**Delivery**: eye contact, steady pace, zaroori jagah pause, voice mein variation. Slides se padhte mat raho.
**Q&A handling**: sawaal dhyan se suno; agar answer nahi pata toh honestly kaho aur baad mein follow up karne ka promise karo.
**GD roles**: initiator (topic open karta hai), contributor (points aur examples), summariser (end mein sab views ka balanced summary).
**GD etiquette**: beech mein mat kaato, polite disagreement ('I see your point, but...'), chup members ko include karo, facts aur examples do.

example.problem: 5 minute presentation ki opening plan kijiye: 'Why first-year students should learn Python early.'
steps: Hook se shuru karo: 'How many of you spent an hour last week doing a calculation that a computer could do in a second?'
Topic clearly bolo: 'Today I will explain why learning Python in the first year pays off.'
Agenda do: 'I will cover three points: saving time, building projects, and preparing for later courses.'
Har point ke liye ek slide: heading + 2-3 short bullets + ek example.
Conclusion ka signpost: 'To summarise, ...' aur phir Q&A invite karo.
Answer: Hook → Topic → 3-point agenda → slides → summary → Q&A, yahi opening aur flow hai.

mistakes: Slides par poora paragraph likh kar padhna. Audience padhne lagti hai aur aapko sunna band kar deti hai.
GD mein dominate karna ya doosron ko beech mein kaatna. Quality points aur doosron ko space dena zyada score karta hai.
Sawaal ka answer na pata ho toh kuch bhi bana dena. Honestly kaho aur baad mein confirm karke batao.
revision: Opening → Agenda → Body → Conclusion → Q&A.
Signposts: 'Let me move on to...', 'To summarise...'.
Slides: kam text, ek idea per slide.
Polite disagreement: 'I see your point, but...'.
Summariser sab views ko balance se present karta hai.
Answer nahi pata toh honestly follow up promise karo.

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to disagree in a group discussion?
options: I see your point, but I would like to look at it differently.
You are completely wrong.
That is a silly idea.
Stop talking and let me speak.
questions.explanation: Pehle doosre ki baat acknowledge karo ('I see your point'), phir apna view do. Ye respectful disagreement hai. Baaki options rude hain aur GD mein negative impression dete hain.

questions.question: Which phrase is best for moving to the next section of a presentation?
options: Whatever, next.
Let me now move on to the second point.
I forgot what comes next.
Okay so, um, yeah.
questions.explanation: 'Let me now move on to the second point' ek clear signpost hai jo audience ko batata hai ki naya section shuru ho raha hai. Baaki options unprofessional hain ya confidence ki kami dikhate hain.

questions.question: In a group discussion, one participant has not spoken for ten minutes. What would a good team player do?
options: Ignore them to save time.
Complain to the moderator about them.
Invite them in: 'Neha, what is your view on this?'
Answer on their behalf.
questions.explanation: Chup member ko politely include karna leadership aur teamwork dikhata hai. Ignore karna ya complain karna negative hai, aur unki taraf se bolna unhe mauka hi nahi deta.

questions.question: Which slide design is most effective for a presentation?
options: Full paragraphs in a 12-point font
Ten bullet points, each in a different colour
Dark blue text on a black background
A clear heading, a few short points and one relevant chart
questions.explanation: Achhi slide mein clear heading, kam text aur ek relevant visual hota hai, taaki audience jaldi samjhe aur speaker par focus kare. Paragraphs aur zyada bullets overload karte hain, aur dark blue on black padha hi nahi jaata.

questions.question: During Q&A, someone asks a question you cannot answer. What is the best response?
options: Make up an answer confidently.
That is a good question. I do not have the exact figure right now, but I will check and get back to you.
Say the question is not relevant.
Ignore it and take the next question.
questions.explanation: Honestly maanna aur follow up ka promise karna professional hai aur trust banata hai. Answer banana galat info failata hai, aur sawaal ko irrelevant bolna ya ignore karna rude hai.

questions.question: What should the summariser do at the end of a group discussion?
options: Briefly present the main views raised, including those they disagreed with.
Repeat only their own arguments in detail.
Introduce a completely new point at the end.
Declare which participant won the discussion.
questions.explanation: Summary balanced honi chahiye: sab main views, chahe aap unse agree karo ya nahi. Sirf apne points repeat karna biased hai, aur end mein naya point lana summary ka kaam nahi. Trap option B hai kyunki bahut log summary ko apna pitch bana dete hain.

questions.question: Which is the best hook to open a presentation on road safety?
options: My topic today is road safety, so let us start with the first slide.
Sorry, I am not very prepared today.
How many of you crossed a road today without checking the signal?
I will now read my slides to you.
questions.explanation: Hook shuru mein attention pakadta hai, jaise audience se seedha sawaal. 'How many of you...?' sabko unki apni real situation se jod deta hai. 'My topic today is road safety' sirf topic batata hai, hook nahi hai, aur maafi maangna ya slides padhna weak opening hai.

questions.question: In a group discussion, the person who opens the topic is called the:
options: summariser
contributor
listener
initiator
questions.explanation: Initiator GD shuru karta hai aur topic open karta hai. Summariser end mein sab views ka summary deta hai, aur contributor beech mein points aur examples deta hai.

questions.question: Which habit is best while delivering a presentation?
options: Reading every word from the slides
Keeping eye contact with the audience
Speaking as fast as possible to save time
Facing the screen most of the time
questions.explanation: Eye contact se audience judi hui mehsoos karti hai aur speaker confident lagta hai. Slides se padhna aur screen ki taraf mooh rakhna audience se connection tod deta hai, aur bahut tez bolne se baat samajh nahi aati; pace steady honi chahiye.

questions.question: Which sentence is an agenda statement in a presentation?
options: I will cover three points: the problem, our survey results and our proposal.
Thank you all for listening so patiently to my presentation today.
Are there any questions?
Did you know that many students skip breakfast before their morning classes?
questions.explanation: Agenda batata hai ki presentation mein kya-kya cover hoga: 'three points: the problem, our survey results and our proposal'. 'Thank you all for listening...' end mein aata hai, 'Are there any questions?' Q&A hai, aur 'Did you know...?' hook hai, agenda nahi.

questions.question: In a GD, one participant keeps interrupting others. What is the most appropriate thing to say?
options: Be quiet, you have been talking far too much in this GD.
Excuse me, could we let Arjun finish his point first?
Everyone, please just ignore him.
Nothing; just wait for the GD to end.
questions.explanation: Politely interruption rokna aur doosre ko poora bolne dena GD etiquette hai: 'could we let Arjun finish his point first?'. 'Be quiet...' rude hai, sabko ignore karne ko kehna negative hai, aur bilkul chup rehna discussion ko unfair hi rehne deta hai.

questions.question: Arrange these presentation lines in the best order: (P) 'To summarise, small daily habits can save a lot of water.' (Q) 'How many litres of water do you think your family uses in a day?' (R) 'I will talk about three habits: shorter showers, fixing leaks and reusing RO water.' (S) 'Let me begin with shorter showers.'
options: R, Q, S, P
Q, S, R, P
Q, R, S, P
P, Q, R, S
questions.explanation: Structure: Hook → Agenda → Body → Conclusion. Q sawaal wala hook hai, R agenda (teen habits), S body ki shuruaat ('Let me begin with...'), aur P conclusion ('To summarise'). Isliye Q, R, S, P. 'R, Q, S, P' mein hook se pehle agenda aa gaya, aur 'Q, S, R, P' mein agenda body ke beech mein chala gaya.

questions.question: In a GD on 'Should attendance be compulsory in online courses?', which contribution adds the most value?
options: I agree with everything that everyone has said so far, so I have nothing more to add.
Compulsory attendance is simply bad, and anyone who supports it is wrong.
This topic is boring, so let us discuss something else instead.
Our quiz scores rose after weekly live sessions began, so some attendance may help.
questions.explanation: Achha contribution point ke saath example ya fact deta hai: quiz scores aur live sessions wala example concrete evidence hai. 'I agree with everything' kuch naya nahi jodta, 'anyone who supports it is wrong' bina reason ka aur rude hai, aur topic badalne ko kehna GD ko patri se utaar deta hai.

questions.question: A speaker finishes a 10-minute talk in 5 minutes. He reads from slides full of paragraphs and mostly stands with his back to the audience. Which change would help him most?
options: Speak even faster and add more text so that nothing is missed
Use smaller fonts so that more points fit on each slide
Slow down, face the audience and keep only key points on the slides
Skip the conclusion and the Q&A so that he does not run out of time
questions.explanation: Teen problems hain: bahut tez bolna (5 minute mein khatam), text-heavy slides, aur audience ki taraf peeth. Sahi option teeno ko theek karta hai: slow down, face the audience, aur slides par sirf key points. 'faster' aur 'more text' problem badhate hain, smaller fonts padhne mein mushkil hain, aur conclusion skip karna structure todta hai.

questions.question: Which response best shows polite disagreement supported by evidence?
options: I see your point, but last semester's feedback showed 70% wanted recorded lectures, so let us keep them.
I see your point, but you are simply wrong about this.
Last semester's feedback showed that 70% of students wanted recorded lectures, so you clearly have no idea.
I completely agree with you on this.
questions.explanation: Do cheezein chahiye: polite tareeka aur evidence. Pehle option mein dono hain: 'I see your point, but...' aur 70% wala feedback data. Doosra polite shuru hota hai par koi evidence nahi deta aur end rude hai. Teesre mein evidence hai par 'you clearly have no idea' rude hai, aur chautha disagreement hi nahi hai.

weeks.title: Interviews and soft skills
weeks.summary: Is week aap interview ki taiyari, 'Tell me about yourself' ka structured answer, STAR method se examples dena, aur teamwork aur communication jaise soft skills dikhana seekhoge.
concepts: **Preparation**: company aur role ke baare mein padho, job description ke key skills note karo, aur apne resume ki har line explain karne ke liye ready raho.
**'Tell me about yourself'**: Present (abhi kya karte ho) → Past (relevant experience/project) → Future (ye role kyun). 60-90 second, life story nahi.
**STAR method**: behavioural questions ke liye. **S**ituation (context), **T**ask (aapki responsibility), **A**ction (aapne kya kiya), **R**esult (kya outcome aaya, numbers ho toh best).
**Strengths aur weaknesses**: strength ke saath example do. Weakness honest ho, par saath mein batao aap use kaise improve kar rahe ho.
**Body language**: seedha baitho, eye contact, natural smile, haath shaant. Online interview mein camera eye level par, achhi light, quiet jagah.
**Soft skills**: communication, teamwork, time management, adaptability, problem-solving, empathy. Ye technical skills (SQL, Python) se alag hain.
**Questions for the interviewer**: role, team ya learning ke baare mein ek-do thoughtful sawaal poochho. 'No questions' kehna interest ki kami dikhata hai.
**Follow-up**: interview ke baad chhota thank-you email: shukriya, role mein interest, ek line mein koi baat jo discuss hui.

example.problem: STAR method se answer banaiye: 'Tell me about a time you worked under a tight deadline.'
steps: **Situation**: 'In my college fest, our team had to launch the registration website two days earlier than planned.'
**Task**: 'I was responsible for the registration form and the confirmation emails.'
**Action**: 'I listed the must-have features, dropped two optional ones, and tested the form with five friends the same night.'
**Result**: 'The site went live on time, and over 600 students registered in the first week without any form errors.'
Answer: Chaaron parts ek ke baad ek bolo; answer 1-2 minute ka ho aur Result mein number ho toh impact clear hota hai.

mistakes: 'Tell me about yourself' mein birth se shuru karke poori family history sunana. Role se relevant present-past-future rakho.
STAR mein Situation par bahut time lagana aur Action/Result jaldi khatam karna. Interviewer ko sabse zyada aapka Action aur Result sunna hai.
Weakness ke liye 'I have no weakness' ya 'I am a perfectionist' jaisa ratta answer dena. Asli weakness + improvement plan batao.
revision: Tell me about yourself: present → past → future.
STAR = Situation, Task, Action, Result.
Weakness = honest + improvement.
Soft skills = communication, teamwork, adaptability, etc.
End mein thoughtful sawaal poochho.
Interview ke baad short thank-you email bhejo.

questions.question: In the STAR method, what does 'A' stand for?
options: Answer
Attitude
Ability
Action
questions.explanation: STAR = Situation, Task, Action, Result. 'A' ka matlab Action hai, yaani aapne khud kya kiya. Baaki words sunne mein relevant lagte hain par STAR ka hissa nahi hain.

questions.question: Which is the best way to begin an answer to 'Tell me about yourself'?
options: I was born in 2005 in a small town, and my father works in a bank.
I don't know, what do you want to know?
I am a first-year data science student who enjoys working with data, and recently I built a small dashboard for my college fest.
Please read my resume; everything is there.
questions.explanation: Achha answer present se shuru hota hai (aap kaun ho, kya karte ho) aur ek relevant achievement batata hai. Birth aur family details role se related nahi hain, aur baaki do options rude ya unprepared lagte hain.

questions.question: Which answer to 'What is your weakness?' is most effective?
options: I have no weaknesses.
I used to hesitate to ask for help, so now I check in with my mentor every week, which has made my work faster.
I am a perfectionist, so I work too hard.
I get angry easily, and that is just how I am.
questions.explanation: Best answer honest weakness batata hai aur saath mein improvement ka concrete step aur result deta hai. 'No weaknesses' unrealistic lagta hai, 'perfectionist' ratta hua cliche hai, aur option D mein koi improvement nahi hai.

questions.question: Which of these is a soft skill?
options: Resolving a conflict between two teammates
Writing SQL queries
Cleaning data in Python
Building a regression model
questions.explanation: Conflict resolve karna interpersonal skill hai, yaani soft skill. SQL, Python data cleaning aur regression model technical (hard) skills hain jo specific tools ya methods se jude hain.

questions.question: At the end of an interview you are asked, 'Do you have any questions for us?' Which reply is best?
options: No, nothing.
How many holidays will I get?
Could you tell me what a typical first month looks like for someone in this role?
What time can I leave the office each day?
questions.explanation: Role aur learning ke baare mein sawaal genuine interest dikhata hai. 'No, nothing' interest ki kami lagti hai, aur holidays ya jaldi jaane wale sawaal pehle hi interview mein galat priority dikhate hain.

questions.question: In a STAR answer, which sentence belongs to the 'Result' part?
options: Our team had two days to fix a failing data pipeline.
I was asked to find out why the daily reports were wrong.
I traced the error to a date-format mismatch and wrote a fix.
The reports became accurate again, and the fix saved about three hours of manual checking every week.
questions.explanation: Result outcome batata hai, aur best tab hai jab usme measurable impact ho ('three hours every week'). Option A Situation hai, option B Task hai, aur option C Action hai. Trap option C hai kyunki usme 'fix' word hai, par wo kaam batata hai, result nahi.

questions.question: Which of these is a technical (hard) skill rather than a soft skill?
options: Working well in a team
Time management
Adaptability
Writing Python code
questions.explanation: Python code likhna ek specific tool se juda technical skill hai. Team mein achhe se kaam karna (teamwork), time management aur adaptability soft skills hain, jo kisi bhi job mein logon aur kaam ko handle karne mein kaam aati hain.

questions.question: Which body language creates the best impression in a face-to-face interview?
options: Folding your arms and looking at the floor
Sitting straight and keeping natural eye contact
Checking your phone between questions
Leaning far back in the chair and avoiding eye contact
questions.explanation: Seedha baithna aur natural eye contact confidence aur interest dikhata hai. Haath baandh kar neeche dekhna nervous ya closed lagta hai, phone check karna disrespect hai, aur bahut peeche latak kar eye contact se bachna casual aur uninterested lagta hai.

questions.question: When you mention a strength in an interview, you should:
options: list as many strengths as possible without examples
say that you are good at everything
support it with a short, real example
talk mostly about your friends' strengths
questions.explanation: Strength tabhi believable lagti hai jab uske saath example ho, jaise 'I am organised: I planned our fest schedule for 40 volunteers.' Bina example ki lambi list ya 'good at everything' kehna khokhla lagta hai.

questions.question: In a STAR answer, which sentence is the 'Task'?
options: I was responsible for getting the registration page working again.
Our college fest website crashed 2 days before registrations opened.
I moved the site to a faster server and fixed the form.
Registrations opened on time, and 500 students signed up on the first day.
questions.explanation: Task batata hai ki aapki responsibility kya thi: 'I was responsible for getting the registration page working again.' Website crash hona Situation (context) hai, server badalna aur form theek karna Action hai, aur 500 sign-ups Result hai. Trap Action wala sentence hai, kyunki usme bhi 'I' hai, par wo kiya gaya kaam batata hai, responsibility nahi.

questions.question: Before an interview for a data analyst role, which preparation is most useful?
options: Memorising a long speech about your childhood
Preparing to talk only about your hobbies
Avoiding any reading about the company so that you sound natural
Reading the job description and noting the key skills it asks for
questions.explanation: Sabse useful preparation hai job description padhna aur key skills note karna, taaki aap apne examples unse jod sako. Childhood ki lambi speech role se relevant nahi, sirf hobbies par focus kaafi nahi, aur company ke baare mein na padhna interest ki kami dikhata hai.

questions.question: A candidate answers a teamwork question: 'In my second year, our group had a project on traffic data. There were four of us, the topic was quite difficult, the deadline was in December, and our guide was very strict. In the end, it went well.' What is the main weakness of this answer?
options: It gives too many numbers and figures in the Result part.
It does not describe any situation or background at all.
It is almost all Situation, with no clear Action or Result.
It focuses too much on what the candidate personally did in the project.
questions.explanation: Answer ka lagbhag poora hissa Situation hai (group, topic, deadline, guide). Candidate ne khud kya kiya (Action) wo bataya hi nahi, aur 'it went well' vague Result hai, koi number ya outcome nahi. Isliye 'too many numbers' aur 'too much on what the candidate personally did' sach ke ulta hain, aur situation toh zaroorat se zyada hai.

questions.question: Which set of choices creates the best impression in an online interview?
options: Camera at eye level, good light, a quiet room, and looking at the camera
Camera below your face, a bright window behind you, and phone notifications switched on
A noisy café with earphones in, looking down at your notes for most of the interview
Camera switched off for the whole interview so that you can read your prepared answers
questions.explanation: Online interview ke liye: camera eye level par, achhi light, quiet jagah. Camera mein dekhna eye contact jaisa lagta hai. Peeche bright window se chehra dark dikhta hai, notifications aur noisy café distraction hain, aur camera band karke answers padhna unprofessional hai.

questions.question: For a data science internship, which answer to 'Tell me about yourself' best follows the present → past → future pattern?
options: I was born in Patna in 2005. My hobbies are cricket and music, my father is an engineer, and my mother is a teacher.
I am a second-year data science student. Last semester I built a bus-delay prediction project, and I would like this internship to work on real data.
Last semester I built a bus-delay project. I am a second-year student. In my free time I like cricket and music, and I play for my hostel team every weekend.
I want this internship. Before this, I studied at school and then joined college. Now I am here for the interview, and I am ready.
questions.explanation: Present (abhi: second-year data science student) → Past (relevant project: bus delays) → Future (internship kyun: real data par kaam). Teesra option past se shuru hota hai aur future (ye role kyun) chhod deta hai. Pehla option family aur hobbies wali life story hai, aur chautha vague hai, usme koi concrete baat nahi.

questions.question: Which thank-you email after an interview is the most effective?
options: Thanks!! It was great talking to u. Hope I got selected. Plz let me know asap.
Thank you. Please find my resume attached again for your reference. Also, what is the salary for this role?
Dear Sir, I am writing to remind you that you have not yet replied about my interview result.
Thank you for your time today. Our talk on dashboard design made me even keener on this role.
questions.explanation: Follow-up email mein teen cheezein honi chahiye: shukriya, role mein interest, aur interview mein discuss hui koi ek baat. Aakhri option mein teeno hain (dashboard design wali baat). 'Thanks!! ... Plz ... asap' informal hai, resume dobara bhej kar salary poochna galat priority dikhata hai, aur result ke liye yaad dilana pushy lagta hai.
